definition_zh: n. 糖尿病；（旧义）虹吸管；尿崩症（diabetes insipidus）
definition_en: a disease in which the body cannot control the level of sugar in the blood
core_image: 血糖仪上数字偏高，试纸尖端一滴血；一个人饭前拿出胰岛素笔
scene: 他患有糖尿病。 He has diabetes.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：diabetes 指糖尿病；句意是他患有糖尿病。

derivatives.zh: 糖尿病的；糖尿病患者的

senses.title: A disease of high blood sugar
senses.titleCN: 高血糖疾病
senses.definition: a disease in which the body cannot control the level of sugar in the blood
senses.definitionCN: 身体无法控制血糖水平的一种疾病
senses.example: He has diabetes.
senses.exampleCN: 他患有糖尿病。
senses.why: A meter showing a high figure beside a used test strip.
senses.whyCN: 一台读数偏高的血糖仪，旁边是用过的试纸。

senses.title: The two main types
senses.titleCN: 两种主要类型
senses.definition: either of the two main forms, type 1 and type 2, with different causes
senses.definitionCN: 两种主要形式（1 型与 2 型）之一，成因不同
senses.example: Type 2 diabetes is more common in adults.
senses.exampleCN: 2 型糖尿病在成人中更常见。
senses.why: Two labelled boxes on a clinic chart.
senses.whyCN: 诊所图表上两个标注的方框。

senses.title: A related water-balance disease
senses.titleCN: 尿崩症
senses.definition: diabetes insipidus, a rarer condition in which the body passes too much water
senses.definitionCN: 尿崩症，一种较罕见的、身体排出过多水分的病症
senses.example: Diabetes insipidus is not caused by sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 尿崩症不是由糖引起的。
senses.why: A jug emptied many times in one night.
senses.whyCN: 一夜之间被倒空多次的水壶。

intro.en: Diabetes comes from Greek diabetes, a siphon, from diabainein, to pass through, dia- through plus bainein to go.
intro.cn: diabetes 源自希腊语 diabetes（虹吸管），来自 diabainein（穿过），由 dia-（穿过）加 bainein（走）构成。

items.en: Bainein meant to go or walk.
items.cn: bainein 意为走、行。

items.en: Diabainein meant to pass through.
items.cn: diabainein 意为穿过。

items.en: Diabetes named a siphon or passing through.
items.cn: diabetes 指虹吸管或穿流。

items.en: Diabetes entered English as a disease name.
items.cn: 十六世纪 diabetes 以疾病名进入英语。

items.en: Mellitus was added for the sweet urine.
items.cn: 十八世纪加上 mellitus，指尿甜。

items.en: Type 1 and type 2 are now distinguished.
items.cn: 如今区分 1 型与 2 型。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dia- through family; the near-meaning group names related blood-sugar terms.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dia-（穿过）家族；近义组是相关血糖术语。

entries.definition: Relating to diabetes, or a person who has it.
entries.definitionCN: 与糖尿病有关的，或糖尿病患者。

entries.definition: A drawing that shows how something works; it shares dia- but uses graphein, to write.
entries.definitionCN: 说明运作方式的图；共享 dia-，但用 graphein（写）。

entries.definition: A line across a circle; it shares dia- through plus metron, measure.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过圆的线；共享 dia-（穿过）加 metron（测量）。

entries.definition: The sugar that the blood carries for energy.
entries.definitionCN: 血液为能量携带的糖。

entries.definition: The hormone that lowers blood sugar.
entries.definitionCN: 降低血糖的激素。

entries.definition: Sweet like honey; the word added to name the sugar disease.
entries.definitionCN: 像蜜一样甜；加在病名后指糖尿病。

normalIntro.en: Diabetes is dia- through plus betes going: what passes straight through, as the old name for a siphon.
normalIntro.cn: diabetes 就是 dia-（穿过）加 betes（走）：直穿而过的东西，这正是「虹吸管」这个旧名的由来。

normal.en: Dia- means through, as in diagram.
normal.cn: dia- 意为穿过，如 diagram。

normal.en: Betes comes from bainein, to go.
normal.cn: betes 来自 bainein，走。

normal.en: Diabetes is uncountable.
normal.cn: diabetes 不可数。

normal.en: Diabetic is the adjective and the person.
normal.cn: diabetic 既是形容词也指患者。

normal.en: Mellitus means honey sweet.
normal.cn: mellitus 意为蜜甜的。

abstract.en: A meter showing a high figure beside a used test strip.
abstract.cn: 一台读数偏高的血糖仪，旁边是用过的试纸。

abstract.en: Two labelled boxes on a clinic chart.
abstract.cn: 诊所图表上两个标注的方框。

abstract.en: A jug emptied many times in one night.
abstract.cn: 一夜之间被倒空多次的水壶。

examples.en: She manages her diabetes with diet.
examples.cn: 她靠饮食控制糖尿病。

examples.en: Diabetes affects millions of adults.
examples.cn: 糖尿病影响着数百万成年人。

examples.en: The test checks for diabetes.
examples.cn: 这项检查筛查糖尿病。

dict_mnemonic.text: diabetes ＝ dia（穿过，与 diagram、diameter 同前缀）＋ betes（走，希腊语 bainein）＝「穿流而过」，古人见病人多尿，借虹吸管之名命名，「糖尿病」。

root: 希腊语 bainein（走）→ dia-＋bainein → diabainein（穿过）→ diabetes（虹吸管）→ 英语 diabetes（糖尿病）

sensesIntro.en: One thing passing through: a test strip, a clinic chart and an emptied jug.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一件穿流而过的东西：一张试纸、一份诊所图表与一只被倒空的水壶。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a meter showing a high figure beside a used test strip with one drop of blood
core.cn: 核心意象：一台读数偏高的血糖仪，旁边是带一滴血的使用过的试纸

branches.en: A meter showing a high figure beside a used test strip.
branches.cn: 一台读数偏高的血糖仪，旁边是用过的试纸。

branches.en: Two labelled boxes on a clinic chart.
branches.cn: 诊所图表上两个标注的方框。

branches.en: A jug emptied many times in one night.
branches.cn: 一夜之间被倒空多次的水壶。

branches.en: Both concern sugar the body cannot control.
branches.cn: 两者都关乎身体无法控制的糖。

branches.en: Both share the old passing-through name.
branches.cn: 两者共享「穿流」这个旧名。

intro.en: Diabetes is dia- plus betes; the through prefix also builds diagram and diameter.
intro.cn: diabetes 由 dia- 加 betes 构成；穿过这个前缀也造出 diagram 与 diameter。

latinIntro.en: Greek dia means through and bainein to go; Latin mel means honey and metrum a measure.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 dia 意为穿过，bainein 意为走；拉丁语 mel 意为蜜，metrum 意为测量。

definition_zh: n. 哮喘（气道慢性炎症，反复喘息、气短、胸闷）；由此产生的喘息状态
definition_en: A long-term condition in which the airways narrow and swell, causing repeated wheezing, coughing and breathlessness; also the resulting state of struggling to breathe.
core_image: 气道像被捏细的吸管，气进出都带着哨音
scene: 他一跑起来就喘，随身带着吸入器。 Running brings on his asthma, so he carries an inhaler.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：asthma 指气道反复发炎变窄的慢性病，即哮喘。

senses.title: The long-term airway disease
senses.titleCN: 长期的气道疾病
senses.definition: a chronic condition in which the airways become inflamed and narrow, so breathing is repeatedly difficult
senses.definitionCN: 气道发炎变窄的慢性病，导致呼吸反复困难
senses.example: Her asthma is worse in cold weather.
senses.exampleCN: 她的哮喘在冷天更严重。
senses.why: The Greek root means to breathe hard, so the word names the effort of breathing rather than the lungs themselves.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根意为「费力呼吸」，所以这个词命名的是呼吸的费力，而不是肺本身。

senses.title: The resulting struggle for breath
senses.titleCN: 由此产生的呼吸困难
senses.definition: the state of wheezing and tightness at a given moment, as in his asthma is playing up
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻喘息与胸闷的状态，如「他的哮喘又闹起来了」
senses.example: The dust brought his asthma back within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 灰尘几分钟内就把他的喘息勾了回来。
senses.why: Speakers slide from the diagnosis to the present feeling, which is why the same noun covers both.
senses.whyCN: 说话者会从诊断滑到当下的感受，所以同一个名词把两者都覆盖了。

intro.en: Asthma is Greek asthma, panting, from azein, to breathe hard, related to the verb for blowing that also gives aer, air.
intro.cn: asthma 就是希腊语 asthma「喘息」，出自 azein「费力呼吸」，与表示「吹」的动词同源，后者也给出 aer「空气」。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to blow or breathe lies behind words for air and for hard breathing.
items.cn: 一个意为「吹、呼吸」的拟构词根，藏在表示空气与费力呼吸的词背后。

items.en: Greek azein meant to breathe hard or pant, the physical effort the disease is named for.
items.cn: 希腊语 azein 意为「费力呼吸、喘」，正是这个病命名所依据的身体感受。

items.en: Greek asthma named panting itself, and physicians used it for the condition of laboured breathing.
items.cn: 希腊语 asthma 本指「喘息」，医生用它指呼吸费力的病症。

items.en: Latin kept the Greek term unchanged, and it travelled through medical Latin across Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样沿用了这个希腊词，它随医学拉丁语传遍欧洲。

items.en: English records asthma from the fourteenth century, long spelled with the th that is now silent.
items.cn: 英语从十四世纪起记录 asthma，长期保留如今不发音的 th 拼写。

items.en: Twentieth-century medicine redefined it as chronic airway inflammation, which changed treatment from relief to control.
items.cn: 二十世纪医学把它重新定义为气道慢性炎症，使治疗从「缓解」转向「控制」。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against three words that only share the opening sound; the near-meaning group separates the symptom from neighbouring lung diseases.
note.cn: 形近组提醒不要与三个只是开头音相同的词混淆；近义组把症状与邻近的肺部疾病分开。

entries.definition: Affected by or relating to asthma.
entries.definitionCN: 患哮喘的；与哮喘有关的。

entries.definition: A dangerous lack of oxygen.
entries.definitionCN: 危险的缺氧状态。

entries.definition: The wasting away of a body part.
entries.definitionCN: 身体某部位的萎缩。

entries.definition: Too few red cells in the blood.
entries.definitionCN: 血中红细胞过少。

entries.definition: To breathe with a whistling sound.
entries.definitionCN: 带着哨音呼吸。

entries.definition: Inflammation of the larger airways.
entries.definitionCN: 较大气道的炎症。

entries.definition: Damage to the air sacs of the lungs.
entries.definitionCN: 肺泡受损的疾病。

entries.definition: The feeling of not getting enough air.
entries.definitionCN: 气不够用的感觉。

normalIntro.en: Asthma comes from a Greek verb for breathing hard, so the word names the effort, not the organ.
normalIntro.cn: asthma 出自一个表示「费力呼吸」的希腊动词，所以这个词命名的是「费力」，不是器官。

normal.en: The th is silent in both accents.
normal.cn: 两种口音里 th 都不发音。

normal.en: Asthmatic is the adjective and the person.
normal.cn: asthmatic 既是形容词也指患者。

normal.en: An asthma attack is one bout, not the disease.
normal.cn: an asthma attack 是一次发作，不是这个病。

normal.en: Asthma is uncountable, so no plural.
normal.cn: asthma 不可数，没有复数。

normal.en: Bronchitis and emphysema are different conditions.
normal.cn: bronchitis 与 emphysema 是不同的病。

abstract.en: Picture a drinking straw pinched in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一根中间被捏细的吸管。

abstract.en: Imagine a whistle sounding on every breath out.
abstract.cn: 想象每次呼气都响起一声哨音。

abstract.en: Think of an inhaler kept in a coat pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象外套口袋里常备的吸入器。

examples.en: Cold air can trigger asthma.
examples.cn: 冷空气可能诱发哮喘。

examples.en: He has managed his asthma for years.
examples.cn: 他多年来一直把哮喘控制得住。

examples.en: The clinic runs an asthma review each spring.
examples.cn: 这家门诊每年春天做一次哮喘复查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音记忆：读作「阿兹玛」，想着「啊——嘶——」那口带哨音的气，就是哮喘 asthma（th 不发音）。

root: 希腊语 azein「费力呼吸」生出 asthma「喘息」，与 aer「空气」同源；拉丁语原样沿用，十四世纪入英语，拼写保留不发音的 th。

sensesIntro.en: The two senses are one narrow straw seen twice: the long-term diagnosis, and the whistling struggle of a particular moment.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一根被捏细的吸管被看了两遍：长期的诊断，以及某个时刻带哨音的挣扎。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an airway pinched like a straw, every breath whistling
core.cn: 核心意象：气道像被捏细的吸管，气进出都带着哨音

branches.en: A chest tighter in cold weather.
branches.cn: 冷天里更紧的胸口。

branches.en: A childhood diagnosis carried for life.
branches.cn: 从儿童期带到成年的诊断。

branches.en: Dust bringing the wheeze back.
branches.cn: 灰尘把喘息勾回来。

branches.en: An inhaler reached for mid-run.
branches.cn: 跑到一半伸手去拿吸入器。

branches.en: One narrowed straw, a diagnosis and a moment.
branches.cn: 同一根变窄的吸管，既是诊断也是一刻。

intro.en: Asthma takes the adjective ending -atic to give asthmatic; the surrounding lung vocabulary is built from bronch-, pneu- and -itis.
intro.cn: asthma 加形容词后缀 -atic 得 asthmatic；周边的肺部词汇由 bronch-、pneu- 与 -itis 搭起。

latinIntro.en: The classical layer is Latin spirare, to breathe, and spiritus, breath; Greek bronchos, windpipe, names the tube involved.
latinIntro.cn: 古典层次是拉丁语 spirare「呼吸」与 spiritus「气息」；希腊语 bronchos「气管」指发病时受累的那根管道。

latinEntries.exampleCN: spirare 产生 respire 与 inspire。

definition_zh: 支气管炎
definition_en: inflammation of the bronchial tubes, causing coughing and tight breathing
core_image: 气管内壁红肿发炎，咳声连连不断
scene: 诊室里老人咳得直不起腰，医生凑近听诊。 The smoker's chronic bronchitis worsened every winter.
sceneCN: 这里 bronchitis 是「支气管炎」（第 1 个义项：支气管黏膜的炎症）；句意是这位老烟民的慢性支气管炎每年冬天都加重。

derivatives.zh: 由 bronchia 加 -al 构成，义为「支气管的」
复合词，义为「支气管炎病区」

senses.title: Inflammation of the bronchial tubes
senses.titleCN: 支气管炎
senses.definition: a disease in which the bronchial tubes are inflamed, causing cough and phlegm
senses.definitionCN: 支气管黏膜发炎的疾病，引起咳嗽与多痰
senses.example: The damp winter brought on another attack of bronchitis.
senses.exampleCN: 阴湿的冬天又诱发了支气管炎。
senses.why: The word is built of bronchia plus -itis, the Greek ending for inflammation.
senses.whyCN: 词由 bronchia（支气管）加 -itis（希腊语「炎症」后缀）直接构成。

senses.title: Acute or chronic form
senses.titleCN: 急性或慢性支气管炎
senses.definition: either a short sharp attack or a long-lasting form of the disease
senses.definitionCN: 该病的急骤短发型或迁延慢性型
senses.example: Chronic bronchitis is counted among the lung diseases.
senses.exampleCN: 慢性支气管炎被归入慢性肺病之列。
senses.why: One disease splits into types by how long it lasts.
senses.whyCN: 同一种病按病程长短分为急、慢两型。

intro.en: Bronchitis is a modern coinage from Greek parts: bronchia plus -itis.
intro.cn: bronchitis 是用希腊语部件新造的医学词：bronchia 加 -itis。

items.en: bronchos meant the windpipe; bronchia named its branches.
items.cn: 希腊语 bronchos 指气管，bronchia 指其分支。

items.en: anatomists kept bronchia as a learned term for the air tubes.
items.cn: 近代解剖学家沿用 bronchia 指支气管。

items.en: physicians formed bronchitis with the Greek -itis ending for inflammation.
items.cn: 十九世纪初医生用希腊语 -itis（炎症）构成 bronchitis。

items.en: the word entered general medical use as the disease grew common in cities.
items.cn: 随着城市发病增多，该词进入通用医学用语。

items.en: bronchitis names both the household illness and a chronic smoker's disease.
items.cn: 如今 bronchitis 既指家常病，也指烟民慢性病。

note.en: Bronchitis sits inside the -itis family of inflammations, next to airway words.
note.cn: bronchitis 属于 -itis 炎症词族，并与一组气道词相邻。

entries.definition: relating to the bronchi
entries.definitionCN: 支气管的，与 bronchitis 同根

entries.definition: the cough typical of bronchitis
entries.definitionCN: 支气管炎的典型咳嗽

entries.definition: examination of the bronchi with a scope
entries.definitionCN: 支气管镜检查，同出 bronchia 词根

entries.definition: inflammation of the joints
entries.definitionCN: 关节炎——同用 -itis 后缀，部位不同

entries.definition: infection filling the lungs with fluid
entries.definitionCN: 肺炎，病位更深，常由支气管炎转重

entries.definition: a condition narrowing the airways
entries.definitionCN: 哮喘，气道狭窄而非感染发炎

entries.definition: inflammation of the voice box
entries.definitionCN: 喉炎，同用 -itis 后缀

entries.definition: inflammation of the windpipe
entries.definitionCN: 气管炎，病位在支气管之上

normalIntro.en: Take bronchia, add the Greek inflammation ending, and the disease names itself.
normalIntro.cn: 取 bronchia，加上希腊语炎症后缀，病名自现。

normal.en: Bronchia + itis: the tubes plus inflammation.
normal.cn: bronchia 加 -itis：支气管加炎症。

normal.en: Arthritis is joints; bronchitis is air tubes.
normal.cn: arthritis 在关节，bronchitis 在气管。

normal.en: Acute strikes fast; chronic stays long.
normal.cn: acute 来得急，chronic 拖得久。

normal.en: Smoker's cough is often chronic bronchitis.
normal.cn: 烟民久咳常是慢性支气管炎。

normal.en: Pneumonia sits deeper than bronchitis.
normal.cn: pneumonia 病位比 bronchitis 更深。

abstract.en: Hear a chest rattle like wet paper being rubbed.
abstract.cn: 听胸腔里像湿纸摩擦般的罗音。

abstract.en: See red, swollen tube walls under the scope.
abstract.cn: 想象镜下红肿的管壁。

abstract.en: Feel the tight band around the chest in cold air.
abstract.cn: 感受冷空气里胸口束紧的感觉。

examples.en: The child's bronchitis cleared up after a week of rest.
examples.cn: 孩子的支气管炎休息一周后痊愈。

examples.en: Damp housing made bronchitis common in the old slums.
examples.cn: 潮湿的住房使支气管炎在旧贫民区很常见。

examples.en: A bad cold can slide into bronchitis if ignored.
examples.cn: 重感冒若不加理会可能转为支气管炎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不『蓉』咳太甚」——支气管炎一犯，咳声「蓉蓉」不断，可「不」能咳「太甚」。

root: bronchitis 由希腊语 bronchia（支气管）加 -itis（炎症）构成，是十九世纪初医生新造的医学词；bronchos 更早词源不确定，一般认为与「气管」的拟声或方言词有关，属存疑假说。

sensesIntro.en: One word covers the inflammation itself and its two main courses, acute and chronic.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个词既指炎症本身，也涵盖急性与慢性两种病程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: red, swollen air tubes forcing out cough after cough.
core.cn: 核心意象：红肿的支气管逼出一阵阵咳嗽。

branches.en: a bout of bronchitis
branches.cn: 支气管炎发作

branches.en: acute bronchitis
branches.cn: 急性支气管炎

branches.en: chronic bronchitis
branches.cn: 慢性支气管炎

branches.en: recover from bronchitis
branches.cn: 支气管炎痊愈

branches.en: smoker's chronic cough
branches.cn: 烟民的慢性咳嗽

intro.en: The -itis ending builds a whole shelf of inflammation names.
intro.cn: -itis 后缀构筑了整整一排炎症病名。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Greek, kept unchanged in New Latin medical Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 构件源自希腊语，经近代拉丁语医学用语原样保留。

items.example: the bronchia branch like a tree

definition_zh: n. 关节炎（关节疼痛、肿胀与僵硬）；关节炎症的统称
definition_en: A condition in which one or more joints become painful, swollen and stiff; a general medical term for inflammation of the joints.
core_image: 手指关节又肿又硬，弯一下就疼
scene: 她手指的关节一到阴天就肿痛。 Arthritis makes her finger joints swell in damp weather.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：arthritis 指关节发炎导致的疼痛、肿胀与僵硬。

senses.title: Inflammation of the joints
senses.titleCN: 关节发炎
senses.definition: a disease in which joints become swollen, painful and stiff, covering many distinct conditions
senses.definitionCN: 关节肿胀、疼痛、僵硬的疾病，涵盖多种不同病症
senses.example: Arthritis of the knee made climbing stairs hard.
senses.exampleCN: 膝关节的关节炎让上楼变得困难。
senses.why: The ending -itis names inflammation, so the word itself tells you the joint is inflamed rather than merely worn.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -itis 表示炎症，所以这个词本身就在说关节「发炎」，而不只是磨损。

senses.title: The daily burden of the disease
senses.titleCN: 疾病带来的日常负担
senses.definition: the practical condition of living with stiff and painful joints, as in managing arthritis
senses.definitionCN: 带着僵硬疼痛的关节生活的实际状况，如「控制关节炎」
senses.example: She manages her arthritis with gentle daily exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠每天温和的运动来控制关节炎。
senses.why: Because the condition is lifelong, the word came to name a whole routine of care rather than a single attack.
senses.whyCN: 由于这种病是长期的，这个词逐渐指整套照护日常，而不只是一次发作。

intro.en: Arthritis is Greek arthritis, from arthron, joint, plus the ending -itis, inflammation: literally inflammation of a joint.
intro.cn: arthritis 就是希腊语 arthritis，由 arthron「关节」加表示炎症的后缀 -itis 构成：字面意思就是「关节发炎」。

items.en: Greek arthron meant a joint, the fitting where two bones meet and move against each other.
items.cn: 希腊语 arthron 意为「关节」，即两块骨头相接、彼此滑动的那个接合处。

items.en: The ending -itis marked inflammation of a named part, as in bronchitis and gastritis.
items.cn: 后缀 -itis 标示某个部位的炎症，如支气管炎与胃炎。

items.en: Greek physicians already used arthritis for joint disease, joining the part to its inflammation.
items.cn: 希腊医生已用 arthritis 指关节疾病，把部位与炎症拼在一起。

items.en: Latin kept the Greek word for joint disease and passed it into medical writing across Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语沿用了这个希腊词指关节病，并把它传进全欧洲的医学文献。

items.en: English records arthritis from the sixteenth century as a general name for painful, swollen joints.
items.cn: 英语从十六世纪起记录 arthritis，作为关节疼痛肿胀的统称。

items.en: Nineteenth-century medicine split the term into rheumatoid disease, wear of the cartilage and gout, each with its own cause.
items.cn: 十九世纪医学把这个统称拆成「类风湿」「软骨磨损」与「痛风」等类型，各有病因。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the joint root together and adds another -itis word; the near-meaning group separates inflammation from wear and from older umbrella terms.
note.cn: 形近组把「关节」词根排在一起，并加上另一个 -itis 结尾的词；近义组把「发炎」与「磨损」以及旧的统称区分开。

entries.definition: Affected by or relating to joint inflammation.
entries.definitionCN: 患关节炎的；与关节炎有关的。

entries.definition: An animal with jointed legs and a hard shell.
entries.definitionCN: 有分节腿与硬壳的动物。

entries.definition: Looking inside a joint with a small camera.
entries.definitionCN: 用微型摄像头查看关节内部。

entries.definition: Inflammation of the appendix.
entries.definitionCN: 阑尾发炎。

entries.definition: Swelling and heat in body tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 身体组织的肿胀与发热。

entries.definition: An older term for painful joints and muscles.
entries.definitionCN: 关节肌肉疼痛的旧称。

entries.definition: A painful joint disease caused by crystals.
entries.definitionCN: 结晶沉积引起的关节疼痛疾病。

entries.definition: Wear of a joint without inflammation.
entries.definitionCN: 关节磨损但不发炎。

normalIntro.en: Arthritis is arthr-, joint, plus -itis, inflammation: the ending tells you which part is inflamed.
normalIntro.cn: arthritis 就是 arthr-「关节」加 -itis「炎症」：后缀告诉你发炎的是哪个部位。

normal.en: The ending -itis always marks inflammation.
normal.cn: 后缀 -itis 一律表示炎症。

normal.en: Arthron is joint, so arthropod means jointed foot.
normal.cn: arthron 是关节，所以 arthropod 意为「分节的足」。

normal.en: Rheumatoid disease and cartilage wear are different conditions.
normal.cn: 类风湿与软骨磨损是不同的病。

normal.en: Arthritis is uncountable in ordinary use.
normal.cn: arthritis 在日常用法中不可数。

normal.en: Arthritic describes both a person and a joint.
normal.cn: arthritic 既可形容人，也可形容关节。

abstract.en: Picture a finger joint swollen and hard to bend.
abstract.cn: 想象一个肿胀的手指关节，难以弯曲。

abstract.en: Imagine stairs that must be taken one at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象只能一阶一阶挪上去的楼梯。

abstract.en: Think of a hinge that has rusted from the inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个从里面锈住的合页。

examples.en: Arthritis stiffened his hands each morning.
examples.cn: 关节炎让他每天早晨双手僵硬。

examples.en: Warm water eased her arthritis.
examples.cn: 温水缓解了她的关节炎。

examples.en: The clinic treats arthritis in older patients.
examples.cn: 这家门诊治疗老年患者的关节炎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arthr-「关节」+ -itis「炎」——关节发炎，就是关节炎 arthritis。

root: 希腊语 arthron「关节」加表示炎症的后缀 -itis 构成 arthritis「关节病」，经拉丁语进入十六世纪英语；同根还有 arthropod「节肢动物」与 arthroscopy「关节镜」。

sensesIntro.en: The two senses are the same inflamed hinge seen twice: once as a diagnosis, once as the daily life built around it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个「发炎的合页」被看了两遍：一次作为诊断，一次作为围绕它建立的日常生活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger joint swollen and hard, painful to bend
core.cn: 核心意象：手指关节又肿又硬，弯一下就疼

branches.en: A knee swollen and hot.
branches.cn: 肿胀发热的膝关节。

branches.en: Fingers stiff in damp weather.
branches.cn: 阴天里僵硬的手指。

branches.en: Gentle exercise every morning.
branches.cn: 每天清晨的温和运动。

branches.en: Stairs taken one step at a time.
branches.cn: 一阶一阶挪上去的楼梯。

branches.en: One inflamed hinge, a diagnosis and a routine.
branches.cn: 同一个发炎的合页，既是诊断也是日常。

intro.en: Arthritis is arthr-, joint, plus -itis, inflammation; the same joint root builds arthropod, arthroscopy and arthralgia.
intro.cn: arthritis 是 arthr-「关节」加 -itis「炎症」；同一「关节」词根还构成 arthropod、arthroscopy 与 arthralgia。

latinIntro.en: The medical layer is Greek arthron, joint, and -itis, inflammation; Latin articulus, a little joint, gives article and articulate beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 医学层次是希腊语 arthron「关节」与 -itis「炎症」；旁边的拉丁语 articulus「小关节」产生 article 与 articulate。

latinEntries.exampleCN: arthron 是「关节」词族的起点。
articulus 产生 article 与 articulate。

definition_zh: 治疗；疗法；心理治疗
definition_en: the treatment of a physical or mental condition, especially without surgery or drugs
core_image: 每周同一时间推开的那扇门：把伤处摊开在有光照的地方
scene: 她在楼下列了整整一周的康复课表。 The knee healed faster after two months of therapy.
sceneCN: 这里 therapy 是「治疗；康复治疗」（第 1 个义项：对身体的非药物系统治疗）；句意：经过两个月的治疗，膝盖好得更快了。

derivatives.zh: 治疗师；治疗专家（therapy 加表人后缀 -ist 构成）
治疗的；有疗效的（同根形容词，经拉丁语进入英语）
有疗效地；治疗上（therapeutic 加副词后缀）
心理治疗（psycho- 加 therapy 复合）

senses.title: Treatment for a physical condition
senses.titleCN: 治疗；康复治疗
senses.definition: a planned programme of treatment for an illness or injury, especially without surgery
senses.definitionCN: 针对疾病或损伤的系统性治疗方案，尤指非手术者
senses.example: The doctor recommended a course of therapy for the shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 医生建议为肩膀做一个疗程的治疗。
senses.why: Care arranged as a programme: the wound is met on schedule, again and again.
senses.whyCN: 被安排成方案的治疗：伤口按计划被一次次照看。

senses.title: Treatment of the mind
senses.titleCN: 心理治疗
senses.definition: treatment intended to relieve mental or emotional problems, usually through talking
senses.definitionCN: 以谈话等方式缓解心理或情绪问题的治疗
senses.example: She started therapy after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后她开始接受心理治疗。
senses.why: Talking becomes the medicine; the door opens weekly to the same room.
senses.whyCN: 谈话成为药；每周推开同一扇门。

senses.title: Anything that comforts or restores
senses.titleCN: 疗愈；抚慰（比喻）
senses.definition: an activity that makes a person feel better, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 使人好受些的活动，比喻用法
senses.example: Shopping, he says, is his weekend therapy.
senses.exampleCN: 他说购物是他周末的疗愈。
senses.why: The medical sense relaxes into daily comfort: anything that soothes is called therapy.
senses.whyCN: 医疗义松弛为日常抚慰：凡能安抚的都被称为 therapy。

intro.en: Therapy comes from Greek therapeia, attendance or treatment, from therapeuein, to serve or care for. The healer began as a servant who kept attending.
intro.cn: therapy 出自希腊语 therapeia「侍奉、照护」，词根 therapeuein 意为服侍、照料。治疗者最初是一位持续照料的服务者。

items.en: Therapeuein meant to serve, to be an attendant; care preceded cure.
items.cn: therapeuein 意为服侍、照料；先有照护，后有治愈。

items.en: Therapeia named the whole attendance: the food, the baths, the watchful nights, not only the drug.
items.cn: therapeia 指整套照护：饮食、沐浴、彻夜看护，而不仅是药物。

items.en: Latin borrowed therapeutice in medical writing, keeping the Greek sense of systematic cure.
items.cn: 拉丁语在医学写作中借入 therapeutice，保留希腊语系统治疗之义。

items.en: English took therapeutic in late Middle English, while therapy itself stayed rare.
items.cn: 英语在晚期中古英语借入 therapeutic，therapy 本身仍罕用。

items.en: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries multiplied the therapies and made therapy the everyday word, mental treatment included.
items.cn: 十九二十世纪各种疗法激增，therapy 成为日常词，并纳入心理治疗。

note.en: The first group follows the caring root into its family; the second separates therapy from the wider cure words.
note.cn: 第一组沿「照护」词根走进词族；第二组把 therapy 与更宽泛的治愈类词分开。

entries.definition: the person who gives therapy; the -ist names the doer
entries.definitionCN: 治疗师；-ist 给行为者命名

entries.definition: having healing power; the older adjective of the family
entries.definitionCN: 有疗效的；词族中更年长的形容词

entries.definition: the playhouse; the seeing root of Greek, not the caring root
entries.definitionCN: 剧场；出自希腊「观看」词根而非「照护」词根

entries.definition: the general word for medical care; therapy names one planned method
entries.definitionCN: 医疗的总称；therapy 特指成套方案

entries.definition: the end result of healing; therapy is the road, cure the destination
entries.definitionCN: 治愈；therapy 是路，cure 是终点

entries.definition: the longer programme of restoring ability; often built from therapies
entries.definitionCN: 康复计划；常由多种 therapy 组成

normalIntro.en: Real links: the Greek serving root, the therapist with -ist, the therapeutic adjective, and shopping as weekend therapy.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：希腊「服侍」词根、带 -ist 的 therapist、形容词 therapeutic、以及被称作周末疗愈的购物。

normal.en: Therapy begins as attendance: showing up, again and again.
normal.cn: therapy 始于照护：一次又一次到场。

normal.en: The therapist is the -ist of therapy: the one who serves the cure.
normal.cn: therapist 是 therapy 的 -ist：执行治愈的服侍者。

normal.en: Therapeutic and therapy share one Greek caring root.
normal.cn: therapeutic 与 therapy 共享希腊「照料」词根。

normal.en: A course of therapy is care arranged on a calendar.
normal.cn: a course of therapy 是被排上日历的照护。

normal.en: Weekend therapy: comfort borrowed the medical name.
normal.cn: weekend therapy：日常慰藉借走了医疗之名。

abstract.en: Healing is mostly attendance before it is medicine.
abstract.cn: 治愈在成为医药之前，大多是照护。

abstract.en: Talking can be dosed like a drug, weekly and on time.
abstract.cn: 谈话可以像药一样按周按时服用。

abstract.en: Every therapy is a scheduled return to the wound.
abstract.cn: 每种疗法都是对伤口的一次定时回访。

examples.en: Six weeks of therapy restored full movement to her wrist.
examples.cn: 六周的治疗让她手腕恢复了全部活动能力。

examples.en: His therapist suggested keeping a daily journal.
examples.cn: 他的治疗师建议他每天记日记。

examples.en: Gardening became her quiet therapy after retirement.
examples.cn: 退休后园艺成了她安静的疗愈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟拉皮」——病痛「瑟瑟发抖」，被「拉」出去做「皮」肤按摩，就是治疗 → therapy 治疗

root: 希腊语 therapeuein「服侍、照料」→ therapeia「照护、治疗」→ 拉丁语 therapeutice → 英语 therapeutic 早入，therapy 后起；同根词 therapist。

sensesIntro.en: From Greek attendance, therapy becomes the planned treatment of the body, then of the mind, then any comfort called healing in daily speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 从希腊的照护出发，therapy 成为人体的成套治疗、心理治疗，再到日常语言里一切被称为疗愈的安慰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scheduled return to the wound, care repeated until it closes.
core.cn: 核心意象：对伤口的定时回访，照护重复直至愈合。

branches.en: Care arranged as a programme for the body.
branches.cn: 为身体安排成方案的治疗。

branches.en: Talking becomes the scheduled medicine.
branches.cn: 谈话成为按时服用的药。

branches.en: Any comfort borrows the healing name.
branches.cn: 任何安慰都可借用治愈之名。

branches.en: Body and mind share the same scheduled attendance.
branches.cn: 身体与心理共享同一套定时照护。

branches.en: The metaphor relaxes the medical sense.
branches.cn: 比喻让医疗义松弛下来。

intro.en: Therapy builds with the agent suffix -ist, the adjective therapeutic, and compounds with psycho-, physio-, chemo- and radio-.
intro.cn: therapy 用表人后缀 -ist、形容词 therapeutic 构词，并与 psycho-、physio-、chemo-、radio- 复合。

latinIntro.en: Greek therapeia reached English through Latin medical vocabulary; the serving root also gave therapeutae, the attendants in ancient temples.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 therapeia 经拉丁医学词汇进入英语；服侍词根还给出 therapeutae「古神庙中的侍者」。

items.example: The therapist works three evenings a week.
items.exampleCN: 治疗师每周工作三个晚上。

items.example: The hot spring has therapeutic value.

items.meaning: treatment of the mind by talk
items.exampleCN: 心理治疗以月计而非以日计。
理疗松开了僵硬的膝盖。
化疗削弱了他的体力，却救了他。

items.example: Occupational therapy taught him to write again.
items.exampleCN: 作业疗法让他重新学会写字。

items.example: The garden works therapeutically on patients.

definition_zh: 抗生素；抗菌的
definition_en: a medicine that kills bacteria or stops them growing, or able to destroy bacteria
core_image: 一个小小的盾牌挡在细胞前，抵御看不见的细菌大军
scene: 药房柜台后，药剂师把药盒递过来叮嘱按时服用。 The doctor prescribed a course of antibiotics for the chest infection.
sceneCN: 这里 antibiotic 是「抗生素」（第 1 个义项：杀灭细菌的药物）；句意为医生为胸部感染开了一个疗程的抗生素。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -gram 构成，义为「药敏谱」

senses.title: A bacteria-killing medicine
senses.titleCN: 抗生素（药物）
senses.definition: a drug, often made by or derived from microorganisms, that destroys bacteria or checks their growth
senses.definitionCN: 一种常由微生物产生或衍生的药物，可杀灭细菌或抑制其生长
senses.example: Penicillin was the first antibiotic to change medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 青霉素是第一种改变医学面貌的抗生素。
senses.why: Greek bios 'life' plus anti- 'against' plus -tic gives 'against life'; the word first meant any life-poisoning substance, then narrowed to bacteria.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 bios「生命」加 anti-「对抗」加 -tic 得「对抗生命」；该词初指一切毒害生命之物，后收窄为对付细菌。

senses.title: Destroying bacteria
senses.titleCN: 抗菌的（形容词）
senses.definition: able to kill bacteria or prevent their multiplication
senses.definitionCN: 能够杀菌或阻止细菌繁殖的
senses.example: The coating has antibiotic properties that keep wounds clean.
senses.exampleCN: 这层涂层具有抗菌特性，可保持伤口清洁。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the original relation: the substance stands against bacterial life.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了本原关系：该物质「对抗」细菌的生命。

intro.en: Antibiotic is built from Greek anti- 'against', bios 'life', and the adjective suffix -tic.
intro.cn: antibiotic 由希腊语 anti-「对抗」、bios「生命」与形容词后缀 -tic 构成。

items.en: The root *gweih3- meant 'to live', the same root that gave Latin vita and Greek bios.
items.cn: 词根 *gweih3- 意为「活」，拉丁语 vita 与希腊语 bios 同出一源。

items.en: Bios meant 'life', and it fills English with biology, biography, and symbiosis.
items.cn: bios 意为「生命」，充斥于英语的 biology、biography、symbiosis。

items.en: Anti- meant 'against, in place of', as in antifreeze and antidote.
items.cn: anti- 意为「对抗、替代」，如 antifreeze、antidote。

items.en: French bacteriologists coined antibiose for life against life: one microbe destroying another.
items.cn: 法国细菌学家造 antibiose，指生命对抗生命：一种微生物毁灭另一种。

items.en: With penicillin in the 1940s, antibiotic named the wonder drugs themselves.
items.cn: 二十世纪四十年代青霉素问世后，antibiotic 用以命名这类灵药。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers anti- and bios words; the near-meaning group gathers germ-fighting substances.
note.cn: 形近组收 anti- 与 bios 词汇；近义组收抗微生物药物。

entries.definition: A protein the body makes against a specific invader; made by you, not in a factory.
entries.definitionCN: 机体针对特定入侵者产生的蛋白；由身体自造而非工厂生产。

entries.definition: The study of life; shares bios with a friendlier prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 生物学；共享 bios，前缀友好得多。

entries.definition: Against decay and infection; ends similarly, but the root is sepsis 'putrefaction'.
entries.definitionCN: 抗感染的；词尾相近，词根是 sepsis「腐败」。

entries.definition: Directed against bacteria specifically, often of soaps and coatings.
entries.definitionCN: 专指对抗细菌，多用于皂类与涂层。

entries.definition: Wider still: against microbes including fungi and viruses.
entries.definitionCN: 更广：对抗包括真菌病毒在内的微生物。

entries.definition: The first great antibiotic, from mold.
entries.definitionCN: 第一种重大抗生素，源于霉菌。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the anti- prefix, the bios life root, and the hospital phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用前缀 anti-、词根 bios「生命」，以及医院常用语。

normal.en: anti + bio + tic: against (bacterial) life.
normal.cn: anti 加 bio 加 tic：对抗（细菌的）生命。

normal.en: Antibiotics kill bacteria, not viruses.
normal.cn: 抗生素杀细菌，不杀病毒。

normal.en: Biology, antibiotic, symbiosis all share bios, life.
normal.cn: biology、antibiotic、symbiosis 都共享 bios「生命」。

normal.en: Antibiotic resistance is when bacteria learn to survive the drug.
normal.cn: antibiotic resistance 指细菌学会在药物下存活。

normal.en: A course means finishing every pill the doctor gave.
normal.cn: a course 指把医生开的药全部吃完。

abstract.en: Picture a shield stamped with a minus sign pressed against a swarm of dots.
abstract.cn: 想象一面印着减号的盾牌顶住一群点状细菌。

abstract.en: Picture a mold dish where a clear ring stops the spreading dots.
abstract.cn: 想象培养皿中一圈透明地带拦住了扩散的点群。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny doorman refusing entry to bacteria only.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小门卫只拒绝细菌入内。

examples.en: Take the full course of antibiotics even if you feel better.
examples.cn: 即使好转也要服完整个疗程的抗生素。

examples.en: Overuse of antibiotics breeds resistant bacteria.
examples.cn: 滥用抗生素催生耐药菌。

examples.en: The ointment has mild antibiotic action.
examples.cn: 这种药膏有温和的抗菌作用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安泰拜奥替」——安泰（安康）靠拜拜奥妙细菌换来，就是「抗生素」

root: 希腊语 anti-（对抗）+ bios（生命）+ -tic（形容词后缀）→ 对抗生命的物质 → 对抗细菌的药物；二十世纪随青霉素普及定型。

sensesIntro.en: From a general life-poison the word narrowed to the bacteria-fighting drug, and gave back an adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: 由泛指的毒害生命之物收窄为抗细菌药物，并回赠一个形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: life turned against life, a poison drawn as a shield
core.cn: 核心意象：以生命制生命，一剂被画成盾牌的「毒药」

branches.en: The pharmacy line: the drug that emptied the fever wards.
branches.cn: 药房线：让发热病房清空的那种药。

branches.en: The material line: coatings and soaps with the same power.
branches.cn: 材料线：拥有同样力量的涂层与皂类。

branches.en: Both stand anti- against bacterial bios.
branches.cn: 两者都以 anti- 对抗细菌的 bios。

branches.en: The narrow line: antibiotics miss viruses entirely.
branches.cn: 界限线：抗生素对病毒完全无效。

branches.en: The resistance line: every use trains the survivors.
branches.cn: 耐药线：每一次使用都在训练幸存菌。

intro.en: The word shows three Greek pieces: anti-, bio-, and -tic.
intro.cn: 这个词含三个希腊成分：anti-、bio- 与 -tic。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin family; the entries record the Greek source words.
latinIntro.cn: 该词没有拉丁词族；条目记录希腊语源头词。

items.exampleCN: 它为 antibiotic 提供对抗义。

items.meaning: relating to, having the nature of
items.exampleCN: 它构成 dramatic 与 antibiotic。

items.example: It forms antibody, the body's own weapon.
items.exampleCN: 它构成抗体 antibody，身体的自造武器。

items.example: It forms biology, the study of life.
It shares bios but means cooperation, not war.
items.exampleCN: 它共享 bios，但意为合作而非对抗。

items.example: It forms antidote, given against poison.

definition_zh: 免疫力；豁免（权）；免除；（对批评等的）不受影响
definition_en: the body's ability to resist a disease, or a legal freedom from a duty, a charge or a penalty
core_image: 一道门把要闯进来的东西挡在外面，同时一张纸写着「免于追究」
scene: 这里指「免疫力」。 Vaccination gives children immunity to measles before they ever meet the virus.
sceneCN: 这里 immunity 指「免疫力」（第 1 个义项：身体对特定病原体产生的抵抗能力）；句意：接种让儿童在遇到麻疹病毒之前就获得了对它的免疫力。图中可辨识物件：疫苗注射器、抗体、病毒颗粒、防护屏障示意。

pos.zh: 免疫力；（法律）豁免权；免除（义务、费用、处罚）；（对批评、影响的）不受影响

derivatives.zh: 免疫的；不受影响的；豁免的

senses.title: Biological resistance
senses.titleCN: 免疫力：身体抵抗特定病原体的能力
senses.definition: the ability of the body to resist a particular infection or toxin, usually because it has met the agent before or been vaccinated
senses.definitionCN: 身体抵抗特定感染或毒素的能力，通常因曾接触该病原或已接种而产生
senses.example: Vaccination gives children immunity to measles before they ever meet the virus.
senses.exampleCN: 接种让儿童在遇到麻疹病毒之前就获得了对它的免疫力。
senses.why: The biological sense is a metaphor from law: the body is treated as a citizen granted exemption from a disease's demands.
senses.whyCN: 生物学义是从法律借来的比喻：身体被当作一个公民，被授予「免于该病索取」的豁免。

senses.title: Legal exemption
senses.titleCN: 豁免：法律上免于某项义务或处罚
senses.definition: a legal freedom from a duty, a tax, a charge or a penalty that others are subject to
senses.definitionCN: 法律上免于他人须承担的义务、税负、费用或处罚
senses.example: The treaty grants immunity from taxation to embassy staff.
senses.exampleCN: 条约给予使馆人员免税的豁免。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: Latin immunitas named a grant that freed a person or a town from public burdens, and English law kept it.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：拉丁 immunitas 指免除个人或城镇公共负担的授予，英国法把它保留了下来。

senses.title: Diplomatic immunity
senses.titleCN: 外交豁免权：外交人员免受当地司法管辖
senses.definition: the protection that keeps diplomatic staff from being prosecuted or sued in the country where they serve
senses.definitionCN: 使外交人员在驻在国免受起诉或诉讼的保护
senses.example: He claimed diplomatic immunity after the traffic accident.
senses.exampleCN: 交通事故后他主张外交豁免权。
senses.why: Envoys cannot do their work if the host state can arrest them, so a narrow legal exemption was made permanent by treaty and given its own name.
senses.whyCN: 若驻在国能逮捕使节，使节便无法履职，于是这项狭窄的法律豁免通过条约被永久化，并有了专名。

senses.title: Immunity from prosecution
senses.titleCN: 免于起诉：以作证换取不起诉
senses.definition: a formal promise that a witness's testimony cannot be used to prosecute that witness
senses.definitionCN: 正式承诺证人所作证词不能用于起诉该证人
senses.example: The witness was offered immunity in exchange for testifying.
senses.exampleCN: 该证人以获得免于起诉为条件出庭作证。
senses.why: Courts need testimony more than they need this one conviction, so the state trades a legal exemption for information.
senses.whyCN: 法院需要证词甚于需要这一桩定罪，于是国家用一项法律豁免来换取信息。

senses.title: Herd immunity
senses.titleCN: 群体免疫：足够多人免疫后间接保护他人
senses.definition: the indirect protection that reaches unvaccinated people when a large enough share of the population is immune
senses.definitionCN: 当足够比例的人群免疫时，未接种者获得的间接保护
senses.example: Herd immunity protects newborns who are too young for the vaccine.
senses.exampleCN: 群体免疫保护那些太小、还不能接种的新生儿。
senses.why: A germ needs a chain of susceptible hosts to keep spreading; when most links in the chain are immune, the chain breaks and even the unprotected are safer.
senses.whyCN: 病原需要一串易感宿主才能持续传播；当链上多数环节免疫时，链条就断了，连未受保护者也更安全。

senses.title: Innate versus acquired
senses.titleCN: 先天免疫与获得性免疫的分野
senses.definition: either the fast, non-specific defence present from birth or the slower, specific defence learned after exposure
senses.definitionCN: 或指出生即有的快速非特异性防御，或指接触后学到的较慢特异性防御
senses.example: Innate immunity stops most germs within hours, long before acquired immunity is ready.
senses.exampleCN: 先天免疫在数小时内就挡住大多数病原，远早于获得性免疫就绪。
senses.why: Medicine split one word into two mechanisms because they differ in speed and memory, and both are described as exemption from disease.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这一个词分成两种机制，因为它们在速度与记忆上不同，而两者都被描述为「免于疾病」。

senses.title: Freedom from a burden
senses.titleCN: 免除负担：不必承担某种费用或责任
senses.definition: a formal relief from a payment or obligation, as in immunity from rent, fees or service
senses.definitionCN: 对某项付款或义务的正式免除，如免租、免费、免服役
senses.example: The old charter gave the town immunity from tolls.
senses.exampleCN: 旧特许状给予该镇免缴通行费的权利。
senses.why: Immunitas in Latin meant 'not performing public service', and the concrete burdens it lifted, money and labour, were the original content of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 immunitas 意为「不服公共劳役」，它所解除的具体负担——钱与劳役——才是这个词最初的内容。

senses.title: Not affected by criticism
senses.titleCN: 不受影响：对批评、压力等无动于衷
senses.definition: the state of being unaffected by criticism, persuasion or pressure, often used ironically
senses.definitionCN: 不受批评、劝说或压力影响的状态，常带反讽意味
senses.example: His immunity to criticism made the interviews difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 他对批评刀枪不入，这让采访很难进行。
senses.why: The legal image is reused for the mind: a person is pictured as shielded from the demands that words make, as if criticism were a charge in court.
senses.whyCN: 法律意象被挪用到心理层面：人被描绘成对言语的索取有屏障，仿佛批评是法庭上的一项指控。

intro.en: Immunity is Latin immunitas, from immunis 'free from public service', built on in- 'not' plus munus 'duty, service'. The medical sense is a later borrowing of the legal one.
intro.cn: immunity 来自拉丁 immunitas，源于 immunis「免于公共劳役」，由 in-「不」加 munus「义务、公务」构成。医学义是对法律义的后来借用。

items.en: Munus meant a duty, a service, an office, and also a gift or a public show; the underlying idea is something owed or performed for others.
items.cn: munus 指义务、公务、职位，也指礼物或公演；底层概念是「为他人所欠或所做的事」。

items.en: Immunis meant 'not performing a duty, free from a burden', and was applied to persons and to towns exempted from taxes or garrison duty.
items.cn: immunis 意为「不服义务、免于负担」，用于被免除税负或驻防义务的个人与城镇。

items.en: Immunitas named the privilege itself: the exemption from public charges and services granted by a ruler or by law.
items.cn: immunitas 指这种特权本身：由统治者或法律授予的、免于公共负担与劳役的豁免。

items.en: English took immunity in the fifteenth century as a legal term for exemption from service, tax or penalty, and the phrase immunity from prosecution grew from it.
items.cn: 英语于 15 世纪引入 immunity，作为免服劳役、免税、免罚的法律术语，「免于起诉」这一说法由此生长出来。

items.en: In the late nineteenth century, as germs were identified, physicians borrowed the legal word for the body's exemption from a disease, and immunity became mainly medical.
items.cn: 19 世纪后期病原被识别后，医生借用了这个法律词来指身体「免于某病」，immunity 从此主要以医学义通行。

items.en: Source uncertainty: an older explanation linking immunis to munire 'to fortify' is repeated in some references but is not generally accepted; the munus explanation is the standard one. The exact first English date is also not firmly fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根解释存疑，仅首见年代存疑）：部分资料把 immunis 与 munire「筑防」联系起来，但这不被普遍接受；学界标准解释是 munus。英语确切首见年代亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds look-alikes and same-family words that differ in part of speech or scope; the second holds legal and medical terms that overlap with immunity.
note.cn: 第一组是形近词与同族词，区别在词性或范围；第二组是与 immunity 语义重叠的法律与医学术语。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'protected or exempt'; it describes a person or state, while immunity names the state itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「有免疫力的、被豁免的」形容词；它描述人或状态，immunity 则是该状态本身的名词。

entries.definition: To make someone immune, usually by vaccine; it names the action, not the resulting condition.
entries.definitionCN: 使人获得免疫，通常通过疫苗；它命名动作，而非结果状态。

entries.definition: The science that studies immune responses; it is a discipline, not a personal protection.
entries.definitionCN: 研究免疫反应的学科，是一门学问，而非个人所受的保护。

entries.definition: From munus 'gift' plus -ficus 'making': generous. It shares the root but not the sense of exemption.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 munus「礼物」加 -ficus「造成」，意为「慷慨的」；共享词根，但没有豁免义。

entries.definition: A formal release from a duty others must perform; it is the everyday legal word where immunity is the privileged one.
entries.definitionCN: 免于他人须履行的义务的正式解除；它是日常法律用词，immunity 则更带特权色彩。

entries.definition: The capacity to withstand an infection or a drug; resistance can be partial and need not involve an immune response.
entries.definitionCN: 抵抗感染或药物的能力；抗性可以是部分的，且不必涉及免疫反应。

entries.definition: In immunology, the failure to attack a particular antigen, including the body's own tissue; it is not the same as defence.
entries.definitionCN: 免疫学中指不对特定抗原发动攻击，包括自身组织；它与防御不是同一件事。

entries.definition: A special right granted to a person or group; immunity is one kind of privilege, specific to obligations and liability.
entries.definitionCN: 授予个人或群体的特殊权利；immunity 是特权的一种，专指针对义务与责任。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'not' + munus 'duty' gives immunis 'not performing duty', hence 'exempt'.
normal.cn: in-「不」+ munus「义务」得出 immunis「不服义务」，进而表示「被豁免的」。

normal.en: The family runs immune, immunity, immunize, immunization, immunology and immunodeficiency.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 immune、immunity、immunize、immunization、immunology、immunodeficiency。

normal.en: Legal phrases and medical phrases use the same word: diplomatic immunity beside herd immunity.
normal.cn: 法律搭配与医学搭配共用同一个词：外交豁免权 与 群体免疫 并列。

normal.en: Latin munus also gives municipal, munificent and common; the same root, other directions.
normal.cn: 拉丁 munus 还衍生出 municipal、munificent、common；同根，方向不同。

normal.en: immunity is the noun; immune is the adjective; do not write 'immunity from' as a verb.
normal.cn: immunity 是名词，immune 是形容词；不要把 immunity 当动词用。

abstract.en: Picture a gate that lets the body's own traffic through but stops every foreign cart.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门，放行身体自己的车流，却拦下每一辆外来车。

abstract.en: Picture a stamped paper that says 'this person owes nothing'.
abstract.cn: 想象一张盖了章的文件，上面写着「此人无欠」。

abstract.en: Picture a chain of people where most links cannot catch the germ, so the germ cannot walk along it.
abstract.cn: 想象一串人，多数环节都抓不住病原，于是病原无法沿链走下去。

examples.en: Immunity after infection may fade faster than immunity after vaccination.
examples.cn: 感染后获得的免疫力可能比接种后获得的消退得更快。

examples.en: The court ruled that his parliamentary immunity did not cover the charge.
examples.cn: 法院裁定他的议会豁免权不覆盖这项指控。

examples.en: Years of practice gave her a curious immunity to stage fright.
examples.cn: 多年练习让她对怯场产生了一种奇怪的免疫力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「immune 免疫的 + ity 名词」——被免除、被挡住的状态 → immunity 免疫力／豁免权

root: 拉丁 munus「义务；公务」→ in-「不」+ munus → immunis「免于公共劳役的」→ 拉丁 immunitas → 英语 immunity（15 世纪法律义，19 世纪起医学义为主）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one grant of exemption: the body exempted from a disease, the citizen exempted from a tax or a suit, the envoy exempted from local law, the witness exempted from prosecution, the herd that shields others, the two mechanisms of defence, relief from a concrete burden, and a mind shielded from criticism.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一份「豁免」展开：身体免于某病、公民免于税负或诉讼、使节免于当地司法、证人免于起诉、群体为他人挡住传播、两种防御机制、具体负担的解除，以及心灵对批评的屏障。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door that keeps something out, and a stamped paper that says 'not liable'.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇把某物挡在外的门，以及一张写着「不予追究」的盖章文件。

branches.en: THE BODY: immunity as resistance, split into the fast innate and the learned acquired forms.
branches.cn: 身体：作为抵抗力的免疫，分为快速的先天型与习得的获得型。

branches.en: THE LAW: exemption from burdens, then the narrower treaty shield of envoys.
branches.cn: 法律：免于负担，然后是更狭窄的使节条约屏障。

branches.en: THE COURTROOM TRADE: testimony is bought with a promise not to prosecute.
branches.cn: 法庭交易：用不起诉的承诺换取证词。

branches.en: THE POPULATION: enough immune links break the chain of transmission.
branches.cn: 人群层面：足够多的免疫环节打断了传播链。

branches.en: THE ORIGINAL BURDEN AND THE MIND: relief from payment, and a person shielded from criticism.
branches.cn: 最初的负担与心理：免于付款，以及一个人对批评的屏障。

intro.en: Immunity is in- 'not' plus munus 'duty' plus -itas, the suffix that turns an adjective into a state; English later rebuilt the family with -ize, -ization and -ology.
intro.cn: immunity 是 in-「不」加 munus「义务」再加 -itas（把形容词变成状态的名词后缀）；英语后来用 -ize、-ization、-ology 重建了整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin immunis and immunitas supply the core; munus also yields municipal, munificent and remuneration, all built on the idea of something owed or given.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 immunis 与 immunitas 提供核心；munus 还衍生出 municipal、munificent、remuneration，都建立在「所欠或所给」这一概念上。

items.example: The law grants immunity to witnesses.
Most adults are immune to this virus.
items.exampleCN: 多数成年人对这种病毒有免疫力。

items.example: The clinic immunized the whole village.
items.exampleCN: 诊所给全村人做了接种。

items.example: Childhood immunization saves millions of lives.
items.exampleCN: 儿童免疫接种挽救了数百万生命。

items.example: Immunology grew fast after the discovery of antibodies.
items.exampleCN: 抗体发现后免疫学迅速发展。

items.example: The patient has a rare immunodeficiency.
items.exampleCN: 这位患者患有罕见的免疫缺陷。

items.meaning: immune attack on the body's own tissue
items.meaningCN: 免疫系统攻击自身组织
items.exampleCN: 自身免疫可以解释关节损伤。

items.meaning: deliberate or disease-caused lowering of immunity
items.meaningCN: 有意或因病造成的免疫力下降
items.exampleCN: 移植患者需要免疫抑制。

latinEntries.meaning: a duty, an office, a gift

definition_zh: 感染；传染；传染病；感染部位；（计算机）感染
definition_en: the entry and growth of a germ inside the body, or a disease caused by such a germ
core_image: 一群微小的病原穿过伤口，进入身体并开始繁殖
scene: 厨房里，有人划伤了手指却没清洗包扎，伤口渐渐红肿。 The wound became red and swollen because an infection had set in.
sceneCN: 这里 infection 指「感染」（第 1 个义项：病原进入体内并繁殖的过程）；句意：伤口变得红肿，因为感染已经发生。图中可辨识物件：伤口、红肿皮肤、病原颗粒、白细胞。

pos.zh: 感染；传染；传染病；感染部位；（计算机）病毒感染；思想的感染（比喻）

senses.title: Invasion by a germ
senses.titleCN: 感染：病原进入体内并繁殖的过程
senses.definition: the process by which a germ enters the body, settles in a tissue and multiplies there
senses.definitionCN: 病原进入身体、定位于某一组织并在其中繁殖的过程
senses.example: The wound became red and swollen because an infection had set in.
senses.exampleCN: 伤口变得红肿，因为感染已经发生。
senses.why: Latin inficere meant 'to put into, to dye', and the medical sense keeps that picture: something is put into the body and spreads through it like dye through cloth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 inficere 意为「放入、染色」，医学义保留了这幅画面：某物被放进身体，像染料浸透布一样在其中扩散。

senses.title: A disease so caused
senses.titleCN: 传染病：由病原引起的一种疾病
senses.definition: a disease caused by a germ, especially one that can be treated or must be reported
senses.definitionCN: 由病原引起的疾病，尤指需要治疗或必须上报的疾病
senses.example: She missed two weeks of school with a chest infection.
senses.exampleCN: 她因胸部感染缺课两周。
senses.why: English uses the process word for the illness itself because the cause and the condition are hard to separate in ordinary speech.
senses.whyCN: 英语用表示过程的词来指疾病本身，因为在日常语言中病因与病况很难分开。

senses.title: Transmission event
senses.titleCN: 传染：病原从一个人传到另一个人的事件
senses.definition: the passing of a germ from one person, animal or surface to another
senses.definitionCN: 病原从一个人、动物或物体表面传到另一处的过程
senses.example: The infection spread through the ward within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 感染在一周内传遍了整个病房。
senses.why: Spread is the most visible part of the process, so the same noun names the event of passing on as well as the state of being invaded.
senses.whyCN: 扩散是这一过程最可见的部分，因此同一个名词既指被侵入的状态，也指传播这一事件。

senses.title: A localised site
senses.titleCN: 感染灶：局限在某一部位的感染
senses.definition: a confined infection in one place, such as a wound, the bladder or a joint
senses.definitionCN: 局限于某一处的感染，如伤口、膀胱或关节
senses.example: The doctor drained the infection in his knee.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把他膝部的感染引流了。
senses.why: Once a site can be examined and drained, the abstract process becomes a countable object, and clinicians speak of 'an infection' in a place.
senses.whyCN: 当一个部位可以被检查与引流，抽象过程就变成了可数对象，临床医生便说「某处有一个感染」。

senses.title: Systemic infection
senses.titleCN: 全身性感染：病原或其产物进入血液
senses.definition: an infection that has spread beyond its starting point into the blood or the whole body
senses.definitionCN: 已超出起始部位、进入血液或波及全身的感染
senses.example: A local infection can become systemic if it is left untreated.
senses.exampleCN: 局部感染若不治疗，可能变成全身性感染。
senses.why: The body is treated as a space with a boundary; when the germ crosses that boundary, the same word gains a severity it did not have before.
senses.whyCN: 身体被看作一个有边界的空间；当病原越过这个边界，同一个词就获得了此前没有的严重程度。

senses.title: Hospital-acquired infection
senses.titleCN: 医院获得性感染：住院期间新发生的感染
senses.definition: an infection a patient acquires during medical care that was not present on arrival
senses.definitionCN: 患者在接受医疗期间新获得、入院时并不存在的感染
senses.example: Hand washing sharply reduced hospital-acquired infections.
senses.exampleCN: 勤洗手大幅减少了医院获得性感染。
senses.why: Hospitals concentrate sick people and invasive devices, so transmission there became a distinct problem with its own name.
senses.whyCN: 医院集中了病人与侵入性器械，因此那里的传播成了有专名的独立问题。

senses.title: Computer infection
senses.titleCN: 计算机感染：恶意程序潜入系统并扩散
senses.definition: the entry and spread of malicious software in a computer system, named by analogy with disease
senses.definitionCN: 恶意软件进入计算机系统并扩散，借用疾病传播的比喻命名
senses.example: The lab lost a week of data to a computer infection.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室因一次计算机感染损失了一周的数据。
senses.why: A program that copies itself inside a host and spreads to others behaves like a germ, so the medical vocabulary was borrowed wholesale.
senses.whyCN: 一个在宿主内自我复制并传给其他系统的程序，行为像病原，于是医学术语被整套借走。

senses.title: Contagion of ideas
senses.titleCN: 思想的感染：观念、情绪在人群中蔓延
senses.definition: the spread of an idea, a mood or a habit through a group, pictured as a disease passing between people
senses.definitionCN: 观念、情绪或习惯在群体中扩散，被想象为疾病在人际间传递
senses.example: Panic is an infection that travels faster than any virus.
senses.exampleCN: 恐慌是一种传播得比任何病毒都快的感染。
senses.why: The metaphor works because both germs and ideas need carriers and both spread faster in close contact, so 'infection' became a word for social contagion.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻成立，是因为病原与观念都需要载体，且都在密切接触中传得更快，于是 infection 成了社会性传染的词。

intro.en: Infection comes from Latin infectio, a dyeing or staining, from inficere 'to put into, to dip, to taint'. The modern medical sense grew out of the idea of a body being stained from within.
intro.cn: infection 来自拉丁 infectio「染色、污染」，源于 inficere「放入、浸入、使染污」。现代医学义正是从「身体从内部被染污」这一意象生长出来的。

items.en: Facere meant 'to make, to do, to put'; it is the verb behind factory, effect and defect, and its past participle factus shaped a large family.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造、放置」；它是 factory、effect、defect 背后的动词，其过去分词 factus 塑造了一个庞大的词族。

items.en: In- 'into' plus facere gave inficere, literally 'to put into'. It was used for dipping cloth into dye, and from that for staining, tainting and poisoning.
items.cn: in-「进入」加 facere 得 inficere，字面即「放入」。它用于把布浸入染料，由此引申为染色、污染、下毒。

items.en: The noun infectio named the act of dyeing or staining, and by extension a taint or contamination, including contamination of the body.
items.cn: 名词 infectio 指染色或污染的动作，并引申为沾染、污损，包括身体受到污染。

items.en: English infection appears in the fourteenth century; plague writing of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries made it a common word for a disease passed between people.
items.cn: 英语 infection 出现于 14 世纪；16、17 世纪的瘟疫文献使它成为指人际传播疾病的常用词。

items.en: In the nineteenth century, when specific microbes were shown to cause specific diseases, infection was fixed to the entry and growth of those organisms.
items.cn: 19 世纪，当特定微生物被证明引起特定疾病后，infection 被固定为这些生物进入并繁殖的过程。

items.en: Twentieth-century computing and social writing extended the word to malicious code and to the spread of ideas, both still felt as metaphors.
items.cn: 20 世纪的计算机与社会写作把这个词扩展到恶意代码与观念传播，两者至今仍被感觉是比喻。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same Latin verb or differing only in ending; the second holds medical and figurative terms that overlap with infection.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在同一拉丁动词上、或只差词尾的词；第二组是与 infection 语义重叠的医学与比喻术语。

entries.definition: To give a germ to someone or something; infection is the process or the resulting state.
entries.definitionCN: 把病原传给某人或某物；infection 是过程或由此形成的状态。

entries.definition: Able to be passed on to others; it describes a disease or a person, not the invasion itself.
entries.definitionCN: 能够传给他人；它描述疾病或人，而非侵入过程本身。

entries.definition: The presence of parasites such as lice or insects on a body or in a place; it is not a microbial infection.
entries.definitionCN: 虱、昆虫等较大寄生虫在身体或某处的存在；它不是微生物感染。

entries.definition: The body's reaction to injury or infection, marked by heat, pain and swelling; it can occur without a germ.
entries.definitionCN: 身体对损伤或感染的反应，表现为热、痛、肿；它可以没有病原而发生。

entries.definition: The passing of a disease by direct or indirect contact; infection is the broader term for invasion itself.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病经直接或间接接触传播；infection 是更宽泛的「侵入」术语。

entries.definition: An abnormal condition of the body with a definite set of signs; a disease may or may not be caused by infection.
entries.definitionCN: 具有一组明确体征的身体异常状态；疾病可能由感染引起，也可能不。

entries.definition: A life-threatening whole-body response to infection; it is the severe end of the infection spectrum.
entries.definitionCN: 对感染产生的危及生命的全身反应；它是感染谱系中最严重的一端。

entries.definition: The stable presence of germs on or in a body without invasion or symptoms; infection implies damage or response.
entries.definitionCN: 微生物在体表或体内稳定存在而无侵入或症状；infection 则意味着损害或反应。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'into' + facere 'put' gives inficere 'put into', the literal origin of infection.
normal.cn: in-「进入」+ facere「放」得 inficere「放入」，这就是 infection 的字面来源。

normal.en: The family runs infect, infection, infectious, infected, infectivity, disinfect.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 infect、infection、infectious、infected、infectivity、disinfect。

normal.en: Fixed phrases name the source: bacterial infection, viral infection, source of infection.
normal.cn: 固定搭配命名来源：细菌感染、病毒感染、传染源。

normal.en: infection is the noun, infect is the verb, infectious is the adjective: choose by grammar, not by sound.
normal.cn: infection 是名词，infect 是动词，infectious 是形容词：按语法而非读音选用。

normal.en: Same word, new hosts: computer infection and the infection of panic.
normal.cn: 同一个词，新的宿主：计算机感染与恐慌的感染。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of dye entering a cloth and slowly taking over the whole square.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴染料落进布中，慢慢占满整块方形。

abstract.en: Picture a small fire spreading along a floor that has not been cleaned.
abstract.cn: 想象一点火沿未清理的地面蔓延。

abstract.en: Picture a mood moving across a crowded room without anyone touching.
abstract.cn: 想象一种情绪穿过拥挤的房间，没有人接触却都染上了。

examples.en: Wash your hands to lower the risk of infection.
examples.cn: 洗手以降低感染风险。

examples.en: The infection responded quickly to antibiotics.
examples.cn: 感染对抗生素反应很快。

examples.en: The company called the leak an infection of its network.
examples.cn: 公司把这次泄露称为其网络的感染。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in 进入 + fect 做／放」——有东西被放进了身体并在里面繁殖 → infection 感染

root: 拉丁 in-「进入」+ facere「放；做」→ inficere「浸入、染污」→ infectio「染色；污染」→ 英语 infection（14 世纪）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one entry: the germ entering and growing, the illness it causes, the passing from person to person, a confined site, a whole-body spread, a hospital form, a computer form, and finally an idea spreading like a mood.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次进入展开：病原进入并繁殖、由此引起的疾病、人际传播、局限的感染灶、全身扩散、医院内的形式、计算机形式，最后是像情绪一样扩散的观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: germs crossing a break in the skin and settling inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：病原越过皮肤的破口，落脚在身体内部。

branches.en: PROCESS AND RESULT: the invasion itself, then the disease it leaves behind.
branches.cn: 过程与结果：侵入本身，然后是它留下的疾病。

branches.en: BETWEEN PEOPLE: the same noun names the event of transmission.
branches.cn: 人与人之间：同一个名词也命名传播事件。

branches.en: FROM A POINT TO THE WHOLE: a wound or bladder can hold it, or it can enter the blood.
branches.cn: 从一点到全身：它可局限于伤口或膀胱，也可进入血液。

branches.en: THE HOSPITAL: crowded care creates its own pattern of spread.
branches.cn: 医院：密集的照护造出自身的传播模式。

branches.en: NEW HOSTS: code and ideas are infected in the same grammar as bodies.
branches.cn: 新的宿主：代码与观念用与身体相同的语法被「感染」。

intro.en: Infection is in- 'into' plus facere 'put' plus -tio, a noun of action; the same pieces build inflect and inject with different verbs.
intro.cn: infection 是 in-「进入」加 facere「放」再加 -tio（动作名词后缀）；同样的部件配不同动词还造出 inflect、inject。

latinIntro.en: Latin inficere, infectio and infectus supply the family; dis- and re- build disinfect and reinfect from the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 inficere、infectio、infectus 提供词族；dis- 与 re- 在同一词干上造出 disinfect、reinfect。

items.meaning: the act of putting something in; invasion by germs
items.example: The infection cleared after ten days.
The virus infects the cells of the throat.
The patient was infectious for five days.
items.exampleCN: 该病人有五天具有传染性。
不同毒株的感染力不同。

items.example: Disinfect the bench before you start.
items.exampleCN: 开始前先给工作台消毒。

items.example: The same strain can reinfect a person.
items.exampleCN: 同一毒株可使人再次感染。

definition_zh: 过敏；过敏反应；（口语）反感
definition_en: a condition in which the immune system reacts too strongly to a harmless substance such as pollen or food; informally, a strong dislike
core_image: 身体把无害的东西当成敌人猛打
scene: 她小时候喝牛奶没事，成年后一喝就起疹子。 Her allergy to dairy appeared only in adulthood.
sceneCN: 这里 allergy 是「过敏」（第 1 个义项：免疫系统对某种物质产生过度反应）；句意为她对乳制品的过敏到成年后才出现。核心画面是身体把无害的东西当成敌人猛打。

derivatives.zh: 相关形容词，义为「过敏的；反感的」
加 -gen 构成，义为「过敏原」
加 -ist 构成，义为「过敏专科医生」

senses.title: An immune overreaction
senses.titleCN: 过敏；过敏反应
senses.definition: a condition in which the immune system reacts too strongly to a harmless substance such as pollen, food or dust
senses.definitionCN: 免疫系统对花粉、食物或灰尘等无害物质反应过强的状态
senses.example: Her allergy makes her eyes water every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 她的过敏让她每年春天都流泪。
senses.why: Allergy was coined from Greek allos, other, plus ergon, work: the body does a changed work, reacting to something it should ignore.
senses.whyCN: allergy 由希腊语 allos「其他」加 ergon「作用」造出：身体做了一种改变的作用，对本该忽略的东西起了反应。

senses.title: A strong personal dislike
senses.titleCN: 反感（口语）
senses.definition: an informal dislike of a thing or activity, used humorously as in an allergy to hard work
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物或活动的非正式厌恶，常带幽默色彩，如说对辛苦工作「过敏」
senses.example: He claims an allergy to any meeting before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 他自称对中午之前的任何会议都过敏。
senses.why: The medical image is borrowed for taste: the person reacts as strongly and as involuntarily as if the thing were a real allergen.
senses.whyCN: 这里把医学意象借用来表达好恶：这个人的反应同样强烈、同样不由自主，仿佛那东西真是过敏原。

intro.en: Allergy is a coined medical word: Greek allos, other, plus ergon, work, named an altered reaction, and a Viennese doctor turned it into a noun in the early twentieth century.
intro.cn: allergy 是一个被造出来的医学词：希腊语 allos「其他」加 ergon「作用」表示「改变了的反应」，一位维也纳医生在二十世纪初把它变成名词。

items.en: Greek allos meant other or different, the root behind allegory and allopathy.
items.cn: 希腊语 allos 意为「其他、不同」，是 allegory 与 allopathy 背后的词根。

items.en: Greek ergon meant work or action, the root of energy, organ and synergy.
items.cn: 希腊语 ergon 意为「作用、工作」，是 energy、organ 与 synergy 的词根。

items.en: The Viennese paediatrician Clemens von Pirquet coined Allergie in the early twentieth century to name any altered immune reactivity.
items.cn: 维也纳儿科医生克莱门斯·冯·皮尔凯在二十世纪初造出 Allergie，用以指任何改变了的免疫反应性。

items.en: English borrowed allergy within a few years, and it quickly replaced older phrases describing unusual reactions to food.
items.cn: 英语没几年就借入 allergy，很快取代了描述「对食物异常反应」的旧说法。

items.en: Today allergy covers both the clinical condition and a joking dislike, with allergic and allergen built from the same stem.
items.cn: 如今 allergy 既指临床病症，也指玩笑式的反感，allergic 与 allergen 都建立在同一词干上。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the allerg- family; the near-meaning group lists other words for a bad reaction to a substance.
note.cn: 形近组保留 allerg- 词族；近义组列出其他表示「对物质产生不良反应」的词。

entries.definition: Having an allergy, or strongly averse.
entries.definitionCN: 过敏的，或强烈反感的。

entries.definition: A substance that triggers an allergy.
entries.definitionCN: 引发过敏的物质。

entries.definition: A doctor specialising in allergies.
entries.definitionCN: 过敏专科医生。

entries.definition: A comparison between similar things.
entries.definitionCN: 相似事物之间的比较。

entries.definition: An excessive immune response.
entries.definitionCN: 过度的免疫反应。

entries.definition: Inability to tolerate a food or substance.
entries.definitionCN: 无法耐受某种食物或物质。

entries.definition: A tendency to react strongly.
entries.definitionCN: 容易起强烈反应的倾向。

entries.definition: A strong dislike of something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物的强烈厌恶。

normalIntro.en: Allergy is allo, other, plus erg, work: the body working differently on a harmless thing.
normalIntro.cn: allergy 就是 allo「其他」加 erg「作用」：身体对无害的东西起了不一样的作用。

normal.en: Allergic is the adjective, allergen the trigger, allergy the condition.
normal.cn: allergic 是形容词，allergen 是诱因，allergy 是病症。

normal.en: Say an allergy to nuts, not an allergy of nuts: the preposition is to.
normal.cn: 说 an allergy to nuts，不说 an allergy of nuts：介词用 to。

normal.en: It is countable, so say two allergies, one to pollen and one to cats.
normal.cn: 它可数，所以说 two allergies，一个对花粉，一个对猫。

normal.en: Food intolerance is not an allergy: it does not involve the immune system.
normal.cn: 食物不耐受不是过敏：它不涉及免疫系统。

normal.en: The joking use keeps to as well, as in an allergy to paperwork.
normal.cn: 玩笑用法同样用 to，如 an allergy to paperwork。

abstract.en: Picture an army attacking a delivery of flour as if it were an invasion.
abstract.cn: 想象一支军队把一车面粉当成入侵来攻打。

abstract.en: Imagine a door alarm that rings every time a friend knocks.
abstract.cn: 想象一个门铃警报，每次朋友敲门都响。

abstract.en: Think of a bodyguard who tackles the postman.
abstract.cn: 想象一个保镖把邮递员扑倒在地。

examples.en: The label warns that the sauce may cause an allergy.
examples.cn: 标签警告这种酱汁可能引发过敏。

examples.en: She outgrew her childhood allergy to eggs.
examples.cn: 她长大后不再对鸡蛋过敏。

examples.en: His allergy to criticism makes feedback painful.
examples.cn: 他对批评的「过敏」让反馈变得难受。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿勒吉」——阿勒（aller）是「别的」，吉（gy）是「作用」：身体对别的东西起了作用，就是过敏。

root: 希腊语 allos「其他、不同」加 ergon「作用」构成「改变了的反应」这一概念，二十世纪初由维也纳医生造为德语 Allergie，英语借入成为 allergy，字面即「对无害之物起了别样作用」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are an overreaction to something harmless: the medical one is the immune system attacking pollen or food, and the joking one is a person recoiling from work or criticism.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是对无害之物的过度反应：医学义是免疫系统攻击花粉或食物，玩笑义是人对工作或批评避之不及。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the body attacking a harmless visitor
core.cn: 核心意象：身体攻击一个无害的来客

branches.en: Pollen treated as an invader.
branches.cn: 花粉被当成入侵者。

branches.en: Skin rising in rash after a meal.
branches.cn: 饭后皮肤起疹。

branches.en: A person dodging every extra task.
branches.cn: 一个人躲开每一项额外任务。

branches.en: A joke about hating early meetings.
branches.cn: 一句讨厌早会的玩笑。

branches.en: Both react too strongly to too little.
branches.cn: 两者都对太小的刺激反应太强。

intro.en: Allergy joins two Greek roots, allo- for other and erg- for work, and the same stem then builds allergic, allergen and allergist.
intro.cn: allergy 拼合两个希腊词根：allo-「其他」与 erg-「作用」，同一词干随后造出 allergic、allergen 与 allergist。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin layer: Greek allos and ergon were joined directly, coined in German, and then borrowed into English.
latinIntro.cn: 该词没有拉丁语层次：希腊语 allos 与 ergon 直接拼合，先在德语中造出，再进入英语。

definition_zh: 外科；手术
definition_en: medical treatment in which a doctor cuts into the body
core_image: 无影灯下，医生戴着口罩专注操作
scene: 他需要做膝盖手术。 He needs surgery on his knee.
sceneCN: 这里 surgery 是「外科手术」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他需要做膝盖手术。

senses.title: Medical operation
senses.titleCN: 外科手术
senses.definition: treatment by cutting into the body
senses.definitionCN: 通过切开身体进行的治疗
senses.example: He needs surgery on his knee.
senses.exampleCN: 他需要做膝盖手术。
senses.why: This is the main medical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的医学义项。

senses.title: A doctor's office
senses.titleCN: 诊所
senses.definition: a place where a doctor sees patients, in British use
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中医生看诊的地方
senses.example: The surgery opens at nine.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所九点开门。
senses.why: This is a British place sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是英式的地点义项。

senses.title: The branch of medicine
senses.titleCN: 外科（学科）
senses.definition: the field of medicine that uses operations
senses.definitionCN: 以手术为手段的医学分支
senses.example: She teaches surgery at the university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学教外科。
senses.why: Here the word names a discipline.
senses.whyCN: 这里指一门学科。

intro.en: Surgery comes from Greek cheirourgia, hand work.
intro.cn: surgery 来自希腊语 cheirourgia，意为手工操作。

items.en: Cheir meant hand.
items.cn: cheir 意为手。

items.en: Ergon meant work.

definition_en: a doctor of medicine, especially one who treats illness with drugs and advice rather than surgery; also a doctor attached to an institution, or a person or thing that heals
core_image: 一位白衣医生先把听诊器捂热，才贴到病人胸口
scene: 诊室的窗半开着，医生把听诊器在掌心捂了一会儿，才贴到老人胸口。 The physician asked a few quiet questions before writing the prescription.
sceneCN: 这里 physician 指「医生」（第 1 个义项：正式称呼的医学从业者）；句意为这位医生先轻声问了几个问题，才写下处方。图中可辨识物件：听诊器、处方笺、半开的窗。

pos.zh: 医生；内科医生；机构医官；医治者

senses.title: A doctor of medicine, used as a formal title
senses.titleCN: 医生；医师
senses.definition: a person who is qualified and licensed to practise medicine, especially when the word is used as a formal or respectful title
senses.definitionCN: 有资格并获准行医的人，尤用作正式或尊敬的称呼
senses.example: The physician listened to her breathing for a full minute.
senses.exampleCN: 这位医生听她的呼吸听了整整一分钟。
senses.why: Greek physis meant nature, and medicine was once studied as part of natural knowledge, so the healer was named after the natural world he read.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 physis 意为自然，医学当年被当作自然之学的一部分来研究，于是治病的人就按他所解读的自然界来命名。

senses.title: A doctor who treats disease without operating
senses.titleCN: 内科医生
senses.definition: a doctor who works mainly through drugs, diet, and advice rather than by cutting into the body
senses.definitionCN: 主要通过药物、饮食与建议治病，而不是切开身体的医生
senses.example: The surgeon sent the patient back to the physician for drug treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生把病人送回内科医生那里接受药物治疗。
senses.why: English long used physic for medicine as a body of knowledge, so a physician was the one who worked through medicine, while a surgeon worked with hands and steel; the two roles split along that line.
senses.whyCN: 英语长期用 physic 指作为一门知识体系的医学，所以 physician 是靠药物医理工作的人，而外科医生靠双手与刀剪，两种角色就沿这条线分开。

senses.title: The doctor appointed to an institution
senses.titleCN: 机构医官；校医
senses.definition: the doctor officially attached to a school, prison, army unit, or ship, and known by that post
senses.definitionCN: 正式受聘于学校、监狱、部队或船只的医生，以其职位为人所知
senses.example: The camp physician signed the health certificate.
senses.exampleCN: 营地的医官在健康证明上签了字。
senses.why: Since the word is a title, an institution uses it for the doctor it appoints, and the sense settles on the post rather than on the individual's skill.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词本身是头衔，机构就用它来指自己聘任的那位医生，义项便落在「职位」上，而不强调个人医术高低。

senses.title: A healer of hurts that are not bodily
senses.titleCN: 医治者；疗愈之物
senses.definition: a person or thing imagined as curing a hurt of the mind or of society rather than of the body
senses.definitionCN: 被想象成能治好心灵或社会创伤的人或事物，而非医治身体
senses.example: Time is the physician of wounds that words cannot reach.
senses.exampleCN: 时间是言语够不到的伤口的医生。
senses.why: Once the word names the healer of the body, it can be carried over to whatever repairs damage, because the picture of the cure travels more easily than the body it first described.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既然指身体的医治者，就能被搬到任何修补损伤的事物上，因为「治愈」这个图像比它最初描述的身体更容易被搬走。

intro.en: Physician comes from the Greek word for nature by way of the Latin and French names for natural science, because medicine was once taught as part of that science.
intro.cn: physician 经由拉丁语与法语中「自然之学」的名称，上溯到希腊语表示自然的词，因为医学当年是作为这门学问的一部分来教的。

items.en: Physis meant nature, and ta physika meant natural things or natural science, including the study of the body.
items.cn: physis 意为自然，ta physika 指自然之物或自然之学，其中也包括对身体的研究。

items.en: The adjective physikos meant natural, and the noun physike named natural philosophy, the broad study that contained medicine.
items.cn: 形容词 physikos 意为「自然的」，名词 physike 指自然哲学，这门宽泛的学问包含医术。

items.en: Latin physica borrowed the Greek noun for natural science, and medieval writers used it for medicine as the healing branch of that science.
items.cn: 拉丁语 physica 借入这个表示自然之学的希腊名词，中世纪的作者用它指其中治病的那一支，即医学。

items.en: Old French fisique meant both natural science and medicine, and fisicien named the person who practised it.
items.cn: 古法语 fisique 兼指自然之学与医学，fisicien 则指从事这一行的人。

items.en: Middle English took the French word as physicion and later spelled it physician; physics went on to mean natural science while physician kept the medical sense.
items.cn: 中古英语把法语词写作 physicion，后来定型为 physician；physics 继续指自然科学，而 physician 保住了医学义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms on the Greek stem for nature and states the discipline each one belongs to; the near-meaning group gathers words for people who treat the sick.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个希腊语「自然」词干上的形式，并点明各自所属学科；近义组收表示治病之人的词。

entries.definition: A scientist who studies matter, energy, and forces; it shares the Greek root with physician but names a different discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质、能量与力的科学家；与 physician 同出希腊语词根，但学科不同。

entries.definition: The science of matter, energy, and motion.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质、能量与运动的科学；物理学。

entries.definition: An old word for medicine, and the base from which the healers title was formed.
entries.definitionCN: 医学的古称，也是「医生」这一头衔的构词基础。

entries.definition: Relating to the body or to material things rather than to the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体或物质事物有关，而非与心智有关。

entries.definition: A person qualified to treat the sick, used as a general title.
entries.definitionCN: 有资格治病的人，用作一般称呼。

entries.definitionCN: 医生，或医学生、医务工作者。

entries.definition: A doctor who performs operations inside the body.
entries.definitionCN: 在身体上动手术的医生；外科医生。

entries.definition: A community doctor who treats ordinary illnesses and refers patients onward.
entries.definitionCN: 在社区看常见病并负责转诊的医生；全科医生。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the Greek noun for nature, because medicine was once a branch of natural knowledge.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在希腊语表示自然的名词上，因为医学曾是自然之学的一个分支。

normal.en: Physician rests on Greek physis, nature, the same stem that gives physics and physical.
normal.cn: physician 立在希腊语 physis（自然）上，与 physics、physical 同用一个词干。

normal.en: The Old French form fisicien meant one who practises physic, and physic was the old English name for medicine.
normal.cn: 古法语形式 fisicien 指「行医的人」，而 physic 是英语里医学的旧称。

normal.en: Physicist and physician look like twins because both grew from physis, but one studies forces and the other treats patients.
normal.cn: physicist 与 physician 看着像双胞胎，因为都从 physis 长出，但一个研究力，一个治病人。

normal.en: Surgeon comes from a different root, which is why hospitals keep the two titles apart on their signs.
normal.cn: surgeon 来自另一个词根，所以医院的牌子上要把这两个头衔分开写。

normal.en: The plural is physicians, and the word is formal: a clinic writes physician where a friend would simply say doctor.
normal.cn: 复数是 physicians；这个词较正式：诊所写 physician 的地方，朋友之间只会说 doctor。

abstract.en: Nature sits inside the name of the healer: the first physicians read the body as part of the natural world.
abstract.cn: 自然藏在医治者的名字里：最早的医生把身体当作自然界的一部分来读。

abstract.en: One ancient word for nature split into two modern jobs, one reading matter and one reading symptoms.
abstract.cn: 一个古老的「自然」之词分成了两份现代职业，一份读物质，一份读症状。

abstract.en: A title of three syllables keeps a distance that the short word doctor does not.
abstract.cn: 三个音节的头衔保持了一种距离，短词 doctor 就没有这种距离。

examples.en: The physician asked a few quiet questions before writing the prescription.
examples.cn: 这位医生轻声问了几个问题，才写下处方。

examples.en: Her family physician has known her since she was a child.
examples.cn: 她的家庭医生从她小时候就认识她。

examples.en: The camp physician signed the health certificate.
examples.cn: 营地的医官在健康证明上签了字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费心诊」——医生为病人费心诊断，physician 就是医生。

root: 希腊语 physis（自然）→ physike（自然之学，含医学）→ 拉丁语 physica → 古法语 fisique 与 fisicien → 中古英语 physicion → physician；与 physicist 同源而异科。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a healer named after nature; from that identity come the formal title, the doctor who works without a knife, the appointed post, and the healing figure in metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「以自然之理治病的人」；由这一身份分出正式头衔、不动刀的内科医生、受聘的职位，以及比喻里的医治者。

core.cn: 核心意象：一位医生先把听诊器在掌心捂热，再贴到病人胸口。

branches.cn: 内科医生看化验单而不是握手术刀

branches.en: a school doctor signing a pupil's form
branches.cn: 校医在学生表格上签字

branches.en: an old book described as a cure for a tired mind
branches.cn: 一本被说成能治心累的旧书

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek adjective and noun as physicus and physica, and these forms stand behind the French word for medicine.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊语的形容词与名词接收为 physicus 与 physica，这两个形式正是法语中「医学」一词背后的来源。

definition_en: a room in a hospital with beds for patients; a person under the care of a guardian; a district of a city

scene: 医院的走廊尽头，护士站亮着灯。 The nurse checked every bed in the children's ward before midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 ward 是「病房」（第 1 个义项：医院里收治病人的大房间）；句意是午夜前护士查看了儿科病房的每一张床。

pos.zh: 名词：病房；受监护人；行政区；看守

名词，义为「看守、狱吏」，由 ward 加施动者后缀构成

senses.title: A hospital room for patients
senses.titleCN: 病房：医院里收治病人之处
senses.definition: a large room in a hospital with beds for several patients
senses.definitionCN: 医院里放有多张病床、收容数位病人的大房间
senses.example: The nurse checked every bed in the children's ward before midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜前，护士查看了儿科病房的每一张床。
senses.why: Old English weard means guard; the room is where patients are watched over.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 weard 意为看守；病房正是被看护之人所居之处。

senses.title: A person under protection
senses.titleCN: 受监护人：处于他人照管之下的人
senses.definition: a person, especially a child, placed under the care of a guardian or court
senses.definitionCN: 尤其指处于监护人或法院照管之下的孩子
senses.example: The lawyer became the ward of her young nephew.
senses.exampleCN: 律师成了年幼侄子的监护人（侄子成了她的受监护人）。
senses.why: The one kept under watch is the ward; guarding names the guarded.
senses.whyCN: 被看守之人即 ward，「守护」转而指称被守护者。

senses.title: A district of a city
senses.titleCN: 行政区：城市划分的选区
senses.definition: a division of a city for elections or administration
senses.definitionCN: 城市为选举或管理而划分的区域
senses.example: She represents the seventh ward on the city council.
senses.exampleCN: 她在市议会中代表第七选区。
senses.why: A guarded and administered piece of the city becomes a district.
senses.whyCN: 城市中被看守与管辖的一块地方，便成了一区。

senses.title: To keep away; defend against
senses.titleCN: 挡开：防避、抵御
senses.definition: to turn aside or prevent something harmful, as in ward off
senses.definitionCN: 使有害之物偏向、无法近身，如 ward off
senses.example: Vitamin C cannot really ward off every cold.
senses.exampleCN: 维生素 C 并不能真正挡住每一次感冒。
senses.why: The guard's act itself becomes a verb: to ward is to stand watch and push harm aside.
senses.whyCN: 看守的动作本身化为动词：ward 就是站岗并把伤害挡开。

senses.title: A section of a prison
senses.titleCN: 监区：监狱内分隔的区段
senses.definition: a division of a prison where prisoners are kept
senses.definitionCN: 监狱内关押囚犯的分区
senses.example: The new wing added three secure wards.
senses.exampleCN: 新楼增建了三个戒备监区。
senses.why: Where guards watch prisoners, the watched place takes the guard's name.
senses.whyCN: 看守监视囚犯之处，被看守的地方便取了看守之名。

intro.en: Ward comes from Old English weard, a watch or guard, from the Germanic root behind guard-words like watch and warden.
intro.cn: ward 源自古英语 weard（看守、守卫），出自日耳曼词根，与 watch、warden 等看守类词同源。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ward- or *war- means to watch over, keep, or guard.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ward- 或 *war- 意为看护、保管、守卫。

items.en: Weard means a watch, a keeper, or a guarding; it stands beside the French-derived guard.
items.cn: 古英语 weard 意为看守、看守者、守卫；与法语来源的 guard 并立。

items.en: Germanic *ward- also entered French, returning as guard, garde, and warder words.
items.cn: 日耳曼词根 *ward- 亦借入法语，以 guard、garde、warder 等形式回流。

items.en: Ward covers guarding, the person guarded, and the act of keeping harm away.
items.cn: 中古英语 ward 兼指看守、被看守者及挡开伤害的行为。

items.en: The hospital sense grows: rooms where patients are watched become wards.
items.cn: 16 至 17 世纪，「病房」义生长：看护病人的房间成为 ward。

items.en: Ward now spans hospital rooms, city districts, wards of court, and warding off harm.
items.cn: 如今 ward 涵盖病房、行政区、受监护人与挡开危险。

note.en: Ward sits at the center of the Germanic guarding family, facing its French double guard; look-alikes share the root, near meanings share the field of watching and protecting.
note.cn: ward 处于日耳曼「看守」词族中心，与法语孪生词 guard 相对：形近组共享词根，近义组共享看护义场。

entries.definition: a person who protects; to protect
entries.definitionCN: 警卫、守卫；与 ward 是同一日耳曼词根经法语的孪生形式

entries.definition: a closet for clothes; a person's collection of clothes
