entries.definition: a prize; to give something officially
entries.definitionCN: 奖品、授予；由法语 esguard 变体而来，与 ward 同根但前缀不同

entries.definition: organized armed fighting
entries.definitionCN: 战争；与 ward 一字母之差且同音，词源为法兰克语 *werra，完全不同

entries.definition: a person legally responsible for someone else
entries.definitionCN: 监护人；与受监护人义相对而相成

entries.definition: to keep someone or something safe
entries.definitionCN: 保护；动作类近义

entries.definition: to guard against attack
entries.definitionCN: 防御；强调抵抗攻击

entries.definition: a place giving protection; to protect
entries.definitionCN: 庇护所；名词近义，强调遮蔽之处

entries.definition: an area of a city or country
entries.definitionCN: 区域、辖区；与行政区义相邻的一般用词

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Germanic guard-root and its French doublet guard.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，来自日耳曼「看守」词根及其法语孪生词 guard。

normal.en: the root means to guard; a ward is a person or place under watch.
normal.cn: 词根意为看守；ward 就是被看守的人或地方。

normal.en: guard and ward are twins: Germanic ward- dressed in French came back as guard.
normal.cn: guard 与 ward 是孪生：日耳曼 ward- 换上法语衣装回流成 guard。

normal.en: ward off keeps the verb sense: push harm aside like a guard.
normal.cn: ward off 保留动词义：像守卫一样把伤害挡开。

normal.en: warden and wardrobe both wear the same old root.
normal.cn: warden 与 wardrobe 都穿着同一古老词根。

normal.en: award is a- plus a related root: what guarding judgment hands over.
normal.cn: award 是 a- 加同根词：看守般的裁断所交出之物。

abstract.en: A lamp burns all night at one door, and behind it someone sleeps unafraid.
abstract.cn: 一盏灯彻夜守在一扇门前，门后有人安睡无惧。

abstract.en: A raised forearm deflects the blow just enough; the guard is the gesture.
abstract.cn: 抬起的小臂恰好把来击挡偏，守护本身就是那个动作。

abstract.en: A city cut into pieces, each piece with its own keeper and its own lamp.
abstract.cn: 城市被切成若干片，每片都有自己的守夜人和灯。

examples.en: The patient was moved from intensive care to a general ward.
examples.cn: 病人从重症监护室转到了普通病房。

examples.en: She raised her arm to ward off the branches.
examples.cn: 她抬起手臂挡开树枝。

examples.en: As a ward of the court, the boy lived with a foster family.
examples.cn: 作为法院监管的孩子，男孩寄住在一个寄养家庭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我德（守德）」——「我守德行，也守着你。」ward 的本义就是守。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自古英语 weard（看守）。

root: 日耳曼语词根 *ward-（看守、守护）→ 古英语 weard（看守、守卫）→ 中古英语 ward。同一词根经法语回流形成 guard、garde，构成孪生词。同族词有 warden（典狱长）、warder（狱吏）、wardrobe（衣柜，字面「守衣之处」）、award（授予）、warden 等；另与 watch 同属守卫词族。

sensesIntro.en: From the guarded door outward: watched rooms, watched people, guarded city pieces, the act of warding off, and the watched section of a prison.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被守卫的门向外铺开：被看护的房间、被监护的人、被管辖的城市片区、挡开的动作，最后到监狱中被看守的监区。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a keeper and the door he watches, on both sides of it
core.cn: 核心意象：看守与他守望的那扇门，门里门外皆有此词

branches.en: Places kept under watch: hospital room and prison section
branches.cn: 被看守之所：病房与监区

branches.en: People kept under watch: the ward of a guardian
branches.cn: 被看守之人：监护之下的 ward

branches.en: The keeper's act: turning harm aside
branches.cn: 看守的动作：把伤害挡开

branches.en: The guarded piece of the city: ward and district
branches.cn: 城市中被看守的一片：行政区

branches.en: Guarding is watching with hands ready to push away
branches.cn: 守护就是睁着眼、随时能把危险推开

intro.en: The Germanic guard-root builds keepers, places, and the act itself across ward, warden, and wardrobe.
intro.cn: 日耳曼看守词根贯穿 ward、warden、wardrobe，构成看守者、被看守之所与动作本身。

latinIntro.en: This family is Germanic, though it returned into English partly through French dress.
latinIntro.cn: 此词族属日耳曼来源，部分词形经法语衣着回流英语。

items.exampleCN: guard 与 ward 的孪生对照

derivatives.zh: 典狱长，由 ward 加施动者后缀构成
狱吏，由 ward 加施动者后缀构成
监护状态，由 ward 加抽象名词后缀构成

definition_zh: 注射；注射剂；（资金的）注入
definition_en: the act of putting a liquid medicine into the body with a needle, or the act of adding money or energy to something
core_image: 一支针筒把药液推进皮肤下面
scene: 诊室里护士正在消毒棉球旁准备器械。 The child cried for a moment, then forgot the injection entirely.
sceneCN: 这里 injection 是「注射」（第 1 个义项：用针把药液送入体内）；句意为孩子哭了一会儿，随后就完全忘了打针这回事。图中可辨识物件：针筒、棉球、消毒盘。

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀还原，义为「注射；注入」
由动词加表示工具的后缀构成，义为「注射器」
由动词加后缀构成，义为「可注射的」

senses.title: Medicine put in by needle
senses.titleCN: 注射
senses.definition: the act of forcing liquid medicine into the body through a needle or tube
senses.definitionCN: 用针或导管把药液压入体内的行为
senses.example: The nurse gave him an injection in the arm.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在他胳膊上打了一针。
senses.why: In- "into" plus iacere "to throw" gives the picture of liquid thrown into the body.
senses.whyCN: in-「向内」加 iacere「投掷」，构成把液体投进身体的画面。

senses.title: The medicine itself
senses.titleCN: 注射剂
senses.definition: a measured amount of liquid medicine prepared to be injected
senses.definitionCN: 预先配好准备用于注射的一份药液
senses.example: The doctor prepared an injection of insulin.
senses.exampleCN: 医生准备了一针胰岛素。
senses.why: The act and the dose share one name, as with many medical procedures.
senses.whyCN: 动作与剂量共用一个名称，这在医疗术语中很常见。

senses.title: Money or energy added
senses.titleCN: 资金或活力的注入
senses.definition: the addition of money, effort, or liveliness to something that needs it
senses.definitionCN: 向欠缺之处补充金钱、努力或活力
senses.example: The cash injection saved the factory.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔资金注入救了这家工厂。
senses.why: Anything pushed forcibly into a weakened system is injected, whether serum or money.
senses.whyCN: 凡是强行推进虚弱体系的东西都算注入，无论血清还是资金。

intro.en: Injection joins a Latin prefix meaning into with a Latin verb meaning to throw.
intro.cn: injection 把拉丁语表示「向内」的前缀与表示「投掷」的动词结合起来。

items.en: Iacere meant "to throw, hurl", and it produced many verbs of projecting and sending.
items.cn: iacere 意为「投掷」，构成了许多表示投射与发送的动词。

items.en: Inicere, from in- plus iacere, meant "to throw in, insert".
items.cn: inicere 由 in- 加 iacere 构成，意为「投入、插入」。

items.en: The noun iniectio could already mean a casting in, including of fluids.
items.cn: 名词 iniectio 当时已可表示「投入」，包括液体的注入。

items.en: French injection carried the medical sense of introducing fluids.
items.cn: 法语 injection 带有引入液体的医学含义。

items.en: English took the word in the fifteenth century; syringes made the medical sense dominant later.
items.cn: 英语十五世纪借入该词，后来注射器的普及使医学义成为主导。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb of throwing; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of putting things in.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「投掷」动词；近义组收其他「放入」的说法。

entries.definition: To throw someone or something out.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「弹出、驱逐」，即向外抛出。

entries.definition: To throw forward, literally or in planning.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「投射、规划」，即向前抛出。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to force liquid or money in.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「注射、注入」。

entries.definition: A preparation given to create immunity, often by injection.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「疫苗」，常通过注射接种。

entries.definition: A measured quantity of medicine taken at one time.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一剂」，指一次服用的药量。

entries.definition: Slow introduction of liquid into the body, or of new life into something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「输液、注入」，强调缓慢流入。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use iacere, the verb of throwing, and the phrases the word occurs in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用表示投掷的 iacere，以及这个词出现的搭配。

normal.en: iacere is to throw: an injection throws medicine in through a needle.
normal.cn: iacere 是「投掷」：injection 是用针把药投进去。

normal.en: Project, eject and inject all throw in different directions.
normal.cn: project、eject、inject 都是朝不同方向投掷。

normal.en: You are given an injection; you do not give it to yourself.
normal.cn: 你是被 give an injection，不会自己给自己打。

normal.en: A cash injection throws money into a struggling business.
normal.cn: cash injection 是把钱投进挣扎中的企业。

normal.en: An injector is the tool; an injection is the act.
normal.cn: injector 是工具，injection 是动作。

abstract.en: Picture liquid meeting the skin's resistance, then passing through it.
abstract.cn: 想象液体遇上皮肤的阻力，然后穿了过去。

abstract.en: Injection is a short, sharp entrance: something outside is forced inside.
abstract.cn: 注射是一次短促的进入：外面的东西被强行送到里面。

abstract.en: A system that is failing can be revived by a sudden push from outside.
abstract.cn: 一个衰败的系统可以被外界突然的一推救活。

examples.en: The doctor gave her an injection to ease the pain.
examples.cn: 医生给她打了一针以减轻疼痛。

examples.en: Two injections a day were needed at first.
examples.cn: 起初每天需要打两针。

examples.en: The company received a large cash injection from investors.
examples.cn: 公司从投资者那里获得了一大笔资金注入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因杰克逊」——因杰克逊医生打了一针，病就好了

root: 拉丁语 iacere「投掷」加 in-「向内」构成 inicere「投入」，名词 iniectio 经法语 injection 进入英语，十五世纪已有记录；同根词有 eject、project、reject、inject。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses come from one image of forcing something in: the act of injecting, the dose injected, and money or energy pushed into a system.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项出自同一个「强行送入」的意象：注射的动作、被注入的药剂，以及注入系统的金钱或活力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a syringe pushes liquid through the skin.
core.cn: 核心意象：针筒把液体推进皮肤。

branches.en: THE ACT: an injection is the moment of forcing liquid in.
branches.cn: 动作这条线：injection 是强行送入液体的那一刻。

branches.en: THE DOSE: the prepared amount is named with the same word.
branches.cn: 剂量这条线：备好的那份药液用同一个词称呼。

branches.en: THE MONEY: cash is injected into a business that needs it.
branches.cn: 资金这条线：钱被注入需要它的企业。

branches.en: THE SPIRIT: new energy can be injected into a dull event.
branches.cn: 精神这条线：活力也能被注入沉闷的活动。

branches.en: THE THREAD: something from outside enters quickly and changes the state inside.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：外面的东西迅速进入并改变内部状态。

intro.en: Injection is a Latin prefix plus a Latin throwing verb, with a noun ending added along the way.
intro.cn: injection 由拉丁语前缀与「投掷」动词构成，中途加上名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin iacere, inicere and iniectio are recorded; the noun form came through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 iacere、inicere、iniectio 均有记录，名词形式经法语传入。

items.example: It sets the direction of the throw.
The root also gives eject and project.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根还给出 eject 与 project。
这是名词背后的复合动词。

definition_zh: 绷带；包扎；护带
definition_en: a strip of cloth used to cover and protect a wound
core_image: 一圈白布条绕在受伤的手指上
scene: 护士清洗完伤口，用一块干净的白布把手指包好。 The nurse put a clean bandage on his cut finger.
sceneCN: 这里 bandage 是「绷带」（第 1 个义项：包扎伤口用的布条）；句意为护士给他割破的手指缠上了干净的绷带。

derivatives.zh: 由 bandage 加 -ed 构成，义为「包扎过的」
由 bandage 加 -ing 构成，义为「包扎、缠绷带」

senses.title: A strip for a wound
senses.titleCN: 绷带
senses.definition: a strip of cloth or other material used to cover and protect a cut or injury
senses.definitionCN: 用来覆盖和保护伤口、割伤的布条或其他材料
senses.example: The nurse put a clean bandage on his cut finger.
senses.exampleCN: 护士给他割破的手指缠上了干净的绷带。
senses.why: The French word meant a strip, so the medical strip that wraps a wound is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 法语词本义是「带子」，所以缠住伤口的医用布条就是第一义。

senses.title: To wrap a wound
senses.titleCN: 包扎
senses.definition: to cover or wrap a wound with a bandage
senses.definitionCN: 用绷带覆盖或缠住伤口
senses.example: She bandaged his knee after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 他摔倒后，她给他的膝盖做了包扎。
senses.why: The verb turns the strip into an action: putting the strip around the injured part.
senses.whyCN: 动词把布条变成动作：把带子绕到受伤的部位上。

senses.title: A support for a joint
senses.titleCN: 护带；固定带
senses.definition: a firm strip worn around a joint to support or protect it
senses.definitionCN: 缠在关节上起支撑或保护作用的结实带子
senses.example: He wears a bandage on his wrist when he plays.
senses.exampleCN: 他打球时手腕上戴着护带。
senses.why: The same strip is used not only for cuts but for support, so protection of a joint is a further extension.
senses.whyCN: 同一条带子不仅用于伤口，也用于支撑，于是又扩展出保护关节的用法。

intro.en: Bandage comes from French and goes back to a Germanic word for a strip.
intro.cn: bandage 来自法语，可上溯到日耳曼语中表示「带子」的词。

items.en: The Germanic verb meaning to bind is the distant source of the strip word.
items.cn: 表示「捆绑」的日耳曼语动词是「带子」一词的远源。

items.en: Old French bande meant a strip or band of material.
items.cn: 古法语 bande 指一条材料或带子。

items.en: French formed bandage for a strip used in dressing a wound.
items.cn: 法语由 bande 构成 bandage，指包扎伤口用的布条。

items.en: English borrowed bandage as both a noun and a verb; the exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语把 bandage 同时借作名词和动词，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The medical sense became dominant, while the general strip sense faded.
items.cn: 医学义成为主要用法，泛指的「带子」义则逐渐消退。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the band family and the strip words; the near-meaning group gathers medical coverings and the act of wrapping.
note.cn: 形近组收 band 词族与表示带子的词；近义组收医用敷料与包扎动作。

entries.definition: A strip that ties or fastens; the direct source of bandage through French.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「带子」，是 bandage 经法语而来的直接来源。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning wrapped in a bandage.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「包扎过的」，由 bandage 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: A strip worn around the head; it shares the strip root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发带」，与 bandage 共享「带子」词根。

entries.definition: A large printed handkerchief worn on the head; it only sounds similar and comes from Hindi.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「印花大头巾」；只是读音相近，词源来自印地语，与 bandage 无关。

entries.definition: A covering placed directly on a wound; broader than a bandage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「敷料」，直接覆在伤口上，范围比绷带更宽。

entries.definition: A small sticky strip placed over a cut; smaller than a bandage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「创可贴」，贴在伤口上的小粘条，比绷带小。

entries.definition: To cover something by folding material around it; the general verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「包裹」，是用材料把东西绕起来的一般说法。

entries.definition: A hard covering that holds a broken bone in place; heavier than a bandage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「石膏固定」，用于固定骨折，比绷带更硬更重。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French origin, the strip image, and the medical phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的法语来源、「带子」意象，以及这个词的医用搭配。

normal.en: Bandage and band share the strip: a bandage is a strip made for a wound.
normal.cn: bandage 与 band 共享「带子」：绷带就是专为伤口做的带子。

normal.en: Put on a bandage is the everyday phrase for covering a cut.
normal.cn: put on a bandage 是处理割伤时最常用的说法。

normal.en: Bandage as a verb simply means to put the strip around the injury.
normal.cn: bandage 作动词，意思就是把带子绕到伤处。

normal.en: An elastic bandage stretches, so it can support a joint without stopping movement.
normal.cn: 弹性绷带可以拉伸，所以能支撑关节又不妨碍活动。

normal.en: Bandage up stresses wrapping the whole area, not just placing a small cover.
normal.cn: bandage up 强调把整片区域包起来，而不只是盖一小块。

abstract.en: Picture a white strip going around a finger three times: each turn is another layer of protection.
abstract.cn: 想象一条白布在手指上绕了三圈：每绕一圈就多一层保护。

abstract.en: The same strip becomes a verb, because a bandage is useless until someone wraps it.
abstract.cn: 同一条带子也能当动词用，因为不缠上去，绷带就没有用处。

abstract.en: A bandage does not heal the cut; it only holds the edges still so the body can heal itself.
abstract.cn: 绷带并不治愈伤口，它只是把边缘固定住，让身体自己愈合。

examples.en: The nurse put a clean bandage on his cut finger.
examples.cn: 护士给他割破的手指缠上了干净的绷带。

examples.en: She bandaged his knee after the fall.
examples.cn: 他摔倒后，她给他的膝盖做了包扎。

examples.en: He wears a bandage on his wrist when he plays.
examples.cn: 他打球时手腕上戴着护带。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「绑得紧」——白布条绑得紧紧，伤口就不乱动：绷带

root: bandage 经法语 bandage 来自古法语 bande「带子」，bande 又上溯到日耳曼语中表示「捆绑」的词根。本义是包扎用的布条，后兼作动词「包扎」，并扩展出支撑关节的「护带」义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of bandage keep one strip in view: the strip for a wound, the act of wrapping it, and a support worn around a joint.
sensesIntro.cn: bandage 的三个义项都围绕同一条带子：包伤口的布条、把它缠上去的动作，以及缠在关节上的护带。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white strip circles an injured finger, layer over layer.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条白布绕着受伤的手指，一圈叠着一圈。

branches.en: THE STRIP: the word names the cloth itself before it names any action.
branches.cn: 布条线：这个词先指布本身，然后才指动作。

branches.en: THE ACT: wrapping the strip turns the noun into a verb.
branches.cn: 动作线：把布条缠上去，名词就变成了动词。

branches.en: THE JOINT: a firmer strip supports a wrist or knee without covering a cut.
branches.cn: 关节线：更结实的带子用来支撑手腕或膝盖，并不覆盖伤口。

branches.en: THE WOUND: the strip and the wrapping exist only because there is a cut to protect.
branches.cn: 伤口线：布条与缠绕之所以存在，只因为有伤口需要保护。

branches.en: THE PRESSURE: a firm wrap holds the edges still and gives the joint support.
branches.cn: 压力线：缠紧的布条固定边缘，也给关节支撑。

intro.en: Bandage is a French formation on the strip word, and English adds only ordinary inflections.
intro.cn: bandage 是在「带子」一词上形成的法语构词，英语只加上普通屈折成分。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic in origin and reached English through French; no Latin cognate is recorded, so the list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源于日耳曼语，经法语进入英语，没有记录在案的拉丁同族词，因此列表留空。

items.example: The strip and the bandage share this root.
items.exampleCN: 带子与绷带共享这一词根。
它由 bande 构成 bandage。
它与 bandage 构成 elastic bandage。
它与 bandage 构成 bandage up。

definition_zh: 温度计；体温计
definition_en: an instrument for measuring temperature, usually a thin glass tube with a scale
core_image: 细玻璃管里的水银柱随冷热升降：热度被翻译成了刻度
scene: 护士把小玻璃管从孩子腋下取出，眯眼看刻度。 The nurse shook down the thermometer before taking his temperature again.
sceneCN: 这里 thermometer 是「体温计」（第 2 个义项：用于量体温的温度计）；句意：护士先甩下体温计的水银柱，再重新量体温。

collocations.phrase: take one's temperature with a thermometer

温度测量法；测温学（thermometer 的学科化名词）
恒温器（同用希腊词根 therm，指自动调温装置）
热的；保暖的（同出希腊 thermos，指与热有关的）

senses.title: An instrument for measuring temperature
senses.titleCN: 温度计：测量冷热的仪器
senses.definition: a device that measures how hot or cold something is, usually with a scale and a liquid column or a sensor
senses.definitionCN: 测量物体冷热程度的装置，通常带刻度和液柱或传感器
senses.example: The oven has a built-in thermometer to keep the heat steady.
senses.exampleCN: 烤箱自带温度计，可以保持温度稳定。
senses.why: Greek thermos means heat and metron means measure: the word literally says a measurer of heat.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 thermos 意为「热」，metron 意为「测量」：这个词字面意思就是「热的量具」。

senses.title: A clinical thermometer for body heat
senses.titleCN: 体温计：量人身体的热
senses.definition: a small thermometer used to take a person's temperature, often placed under the tongue or arm
senses.definitionCN: 用于量人体温的小温度计，常放在舌下或腋下
senses.example: The thermometer showed a fever of thirty-nine degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 体温计显示出三十九度的高烧。
senses.why: When the measurer of heat is applied to a patient, the instrument borrows the name of its most familiar task.
senses.whyCN: 当量热的仪器用到病人身上时，仪器便借用了它最熟悉的任务之名。

senses.title: A gauge of mood or trend
senses.titleCN: 晴雨表：比喻冷热的指针
senses.definition: something that shows or reflects the level of feeling, activity, or public opinion, like a temperature reading
senses.definitionCN: 反映情绪、活动或舆论高低的指标，如同温度读数
senses.example: Sales figures are a good thermometer of customer trust.
senses.exampleCN: 销售数据是顾客信任度的一支晴雨表。
senses.why: Because the instrument turns invisible heat into a visible number, any measure that makes a hidden mood visible can be called by its name.
senses.whyCN: 因为这仪器把看不见的热变成看得见的数字，任何把隐藏情绪显形化的度量都可借用其名。

intro.en: Thermometer is a pure Greek compound: thermos, hot, plus metron, measure. It was coined in the scientific age of the seventeenth century, when measuring heat became a discipline.
intro.cn: thermometer 是纯希腊语复合词：thermos「热」加 metron「测量」。它诞生于十七世纪的科学时代，那时测量热度成为一门学问。

items.en: Thermos meant warm or hot in ancient Greek, and metron meant a measure. Both were common building blocks of learned words.
items.cn: 古希腊语 thermos 意为「温热的」，metron 意为「度量」。两者都是学术用词的常用构件。

items.en: The instrument itself appeared in the seventeenth century, after Galileo's thermoscope showed heat by the rise of water in a tube.
items.cn: 这种仪器出现于十七世纪；此前伽利略的验温器已能用管中水柱的升降显示热度。

items.en: The word thermometer is first recorded in English in the early seventeenth century, as scientists argued about who invented the device.
items.cn: thermometer 一词于十七世纪初见于英语记录，当时科学家还在争论谁发明了这种仪器。

items.en: French thermomtre shows the same learned coinage, and the word travelled between the two languages during the scientific revolution.
items.cn: 法语 thermomètre 是同样的学术造词，科学革命期间该词在英法两种语言间往来。

items.en: The clinical sense narrowed in the nineteenth century, when taking a patient's temperature became routine medical practice.
items.cn: 十九世纪，随量体温成为常规医疗，该词 narrowed 到体温计一义。

items.en: Modern use extends the word to figurative gauges of opinion and mood, keeping the image of a visible reading of hidden heat.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个词延伸到舆论与情绪的比喻性指标，保留了「把隐热显形」的意象。

note.en: The first group holds the therm- word family from Greek; the second gathers instruments and measures that share its job.
note.cn: 第一组是源自希腊语的 therm- 词族；第二组是与它功能相近的量具类词。

entries.definitionCN: 恒温器：通过开关加热来保持温度稳定的装置

entries.definition: relating to heat, as in thermal underwear or a thermal spring
entries.definitionCN: 热的；保暖的，如 thermal underwear 保暖内衣

entries.definition: a vacuum flask that keeps drinks hot or cold; originally a trade name
entries.definitionCN: 保温瓶；源自同一词根，原为商标名

entries.definition: an instrument that measures amount or level, such as a fuel gauge
entries.definitionCN: 计量表；量规，如油量表

entries.definition: an instrument measuring air pressure, often used figuratively for a sign of change
entries.definitionCN: 气压计；常喻指形势变化的标志

entries.definition: the marked series of numbers on a measuring instrument
entries.definitionCN: 刻度；量具上的标度系列

normalIntro.en: Real roots: Greek thermos for heat and metron for measure, plus the therm- family in English.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根：希腊语 thermos「热」、metron「测量」，以及英语中的 therm- 词族。

normal.en: Thermos means hot, metron means measure: thermometer is a heat measurer.
normal.cn: thermos 是热，metron 是测量：thermometer 就是量热的仪器。

normal.en: A thermostat holds temperature; a thermometer only tells it.
normal.cn: thermostat 控温，thermometer 只报温。

normal.en: Thermal underwear and a thermos flask both keep heat where you want it.
normal.cn: 保暖内衣和保温瓶都把热留在你想留的地方。

normal.en: Under the tongue, under the arm: the clinical thermometer waits for your heat.
normal.cn: 舌下、腋下：体温计在等你的热度。

normal.en: Sales as a thermometer of trust: invisible feelings become visible numbers.
normal.cn: 销量是信任的晴雨表：看不见的情绪变成看得见的数字。

abstract.en: A thin glass tube that translates heat into a number.
abstract.cn: 一根把热度翻译成数字的细玻璃管。

abstract.en: The little line that climbs is the fever's confession.
abstract.cn: 那根上升的小线，是发烧的供词。

abstract.en: Every organization keeps a thermometer stuck in the mood of its people.
abstract.cn: 每个组织都把一支温度计插在成员的情绪里。

examples.en: She put the thermometer under her tongue and waited.
examples.cn: 她把体温计放在舌下等着。

examples.en: Check the outdoor thermometer before you water the plants.
examples.cn: 浇水前先看看室外温度计。

examples.en: Thermal cameras work where a normal thermometer cannot reach.
examples.cn: 热成像仪能派上普通温度计到不了用场的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟莫米特」——瑟瑟发抖怕冷热，拿「米尺」来量一量 → thermometer 温度计

root: 希腊语 thermos「热」+ metron「测量」→ 十七世纪科学造词，直译「量热器」；同族词 thermostat、thermal、thermos 均出 therm- 词根。

sensesIntro.en: Thermometer names the heat measurer itself, then the clinical version for body temperature, and finally any visible gauge of hidden feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: thermometer 先指量热仪器本身，再指量体温的临床款，最后泛指任何把隐形情绪显形化的指标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin tube turning invisible heat into a visible number.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细管把看不见的热变成看得见的数字。

branches.en: The instrument that measures hot and cold.
branches.cn: 测量冷热的仪器本身。

branches.en: The small version that reads a patient's fever.
branches.cn: 读取病人体温的小型版本。

branches.en: The borrowed name for any measure of mood or trend.
branches.cn: 借来指称情绪或趋势度量的名字。

branches.en: Both senses rest on one image: heat made readable.
branches.cn: 两个义项立于同一意象：让热变得可读。

branches.en: The figurative sense keeps the picture of a needle climbing with feeling.
branches.cn: 比喻义保留指针随情绪攀升的画面。

intro.en: Thermometer is built from two Greek roots, thermos and metron, and anchors a large therm- family of learned English words.
intro.cn: thermometer 由两个希腊词根 thermos 与 metron 构成，并支撑起英语中庞大的学术词族 therm-。

latinIntro.en: The source is Greek rather than Latin; the learned family below shares the Greek root thermos, so the strictly Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词源是希腊语而非拉丁语；下表学术词族共享希腊词根 thermos，因此严格意义上的拉丁词条留空。

items.meaningCN: 温度计（连接元音 o 接合两个词根）
items.example: Read the thermometer at eye level.
items.exampleCN: 读温度计时要平视刻度。

items.meaningCN: 恒温器（stat 出自希腊语「站立、固定」）
items.example: The thermostat keeps the room at twenty degrees.
items.exampleCN: 恒温器把房间保持在二十度。

items.meaning: the physics of heat and energy

热的；保暖的（形容词后缀 -al）
速度计（与 thermometer 平行的 -meter 构词）
items.exampleCN: 速度计的指针跳了一下。

definition_zh: 脉搏；脉冲；搏动；脉动；活力
definition_en: the regular beating of blood in the arteries, a short sharp burst of electricity or sound, the act of throbbing, and the lively beat of a place or group
core_image: 指尖按在手腕内侧，皮肤下有一记一记的跳动传上来
scene: 手指压在手腕内侧，安静的房间里，那串规律的小跳动先慢后快。 The doctor counted her pulse and wrote the number on the chart.
sceneCN: 这里 pulse 是「脉搏」（第 1 个义项：血液被心脏压入动脉时的规律搏动）；句意为医生数了她的脉搏，把数字写在病历上。图中可辨识物件：按在腕上的指尖、病历夹、笔。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 puls- 加动词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「有规律地搏动」
由 pulsate 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「搏动；脉动」
由表示「向内」的前缀 im- 加拉丁 pulsus 构成，义为「冲动；推动力」

senses.title: The regular beat of blood in the arteries
senses.titleCN: 脉搏
senses.definition: the regular beating of blood that can be felt at the wrist or neck as the heart pumps
senses.definitionCN: 心脏泵血时在手腕或颈部能摸到的规律搏动
senses.example: The nurse felt for a pulse at his wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在他手腕上摸脉搏。
senses.why: Latin pulsus meant a beat or a blow, so the word names the little hammering that the heart sends out along the arteries.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pulsus 意为「敲击、打击」，所以这个词指心脏顺着动脉送出的那一下下敲击。

senses.title: A short sharp burst of electricity or sound
senses.titleCN: 脉冲
senses.definition: a brief, sharp surge of electrical current, light or sound that rises and falls quickly
senses.definitionCN: 电流、光或声音短暂而尖锐的一次起落
senses.example: The device sends a pulse every second.
senses.exampleCN: 这个装置每秒发出一个脉冲。
senses.why: A pulse in physics is one beat of a signal, and the sense comes straight from the beating of the heart: a single rise and fall, then silence.
senses.whyCN: 物理学里的脉冲是信号的一记跳动，这个义项直接来自心跳：一次起落，然后是静默。

senses.title: The steady life or energy of a place or group
senses.titleCN: 脉动；活力；气氛
senses.definition: the lively, continuing energy that a place, group or activity seems to have
senses.definitionCN: 某个地方、群体或活动呈现出的持续生气与律动
senses.example: He could feel the pulse of the crowd quicken.
senses.exampleCN: 他能感到人群的脉动加快了。
senses.why: A busy street or a crowd beats with small movements the way a body does, so the medical word is borrowed for collective energy.
senses.whyCN: 热闹的街道或人群像身体一样以小动作跳动，于是这个医学词被借去指集体的活力。

senses.title: To beat or throb regularly
senses.titleCN: 搏动；跳动
senses.definition: to beat or throb with a regular rhythm, as blood or music does
senses.definitionCN: 像血液或音乐那样按规律节奏跳动
senses.example: The music pulsed through the floor of the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐透过大厅的地板一下下震动。
senses.why: The verb is the noun turned into action: whatever produces a pulse can be said to pulse, from an artery to a bass line.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词转成动作：凡能产生一次搏动的东西，都能说 pulse，从动脉到低音节奏皆是如此。

intro.en: Pulse comes through Old French from Latin pulsus, a beat or a blow, which is the past participle of pellere, to drive or strike.
intro.cn: pulse 经古法语来自拉丁语 pulsus（敲打、跳动），而 pulsus 是动词 pellere（推动、击打）的过去分词。

items.en: Pellere meant to drive, push or strike, and it supplied the family of beating words in Latin.
items.cn: pellere 意为推动、撞击，拉丁语中一整族表示「跳动、敲打」的词都由它派生。

items.en: Pulsus, the past participle, meant a beat or a blow, and was used for the beating of the heart and of the pulse.
items.cn: 过去分词 pulsus 意为敲击、跳动，用来指心脏和脉管的搏动。

items.en: Old French took the noun as pouls or puls, keeping the medical sense of the beat felt at the wrist.
items.cn: 古法语把名词写作 pouls 或 puls，保留了「腕上能摸到的搏动」这一医学义。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word as pulse and used it both for the heartbeat and for a measured beat in general.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 pulse，既指心跳，也泛指有节律的敲击。

items.en: Modern English extends pulse to electrical and sound signals, to any lively rhythm, and to the verb meaning to throb.
items.cn: 现代英语把 pulse 扩展到电信号与声信号、任何有生气的节奏，以及表示「搏动」的动词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that share the shape of pulse but not its history; the near-meaning group collects other words for a regular beat.
note.cn: 形近组收外形与 pulse 相近但并不同源的词；近义组收其他表示规律跳动的词。

entries.definition: A small bag for money, or to draw the lips tight.
entries.definitionCN: 装钱的小包，或把嘴唇收紧。

entries.definition: Added to; also the sign that marks addition.
entries.definitionCN: 加上；也指表示加号的符号。

entries.definition: To follow someone or something in order to catch it.
entries.definitionCN: 为了抓住而追赶。

entries.definition: A star that sends out regular radio pulses.
entries.definitionCN: 规律发出射电脉冲的星体。

entries.definition: To strike repeatedly, or a regular stroke of sound.
entries.definitionCN: 反复敲击，或规律的一记声响。

entries.definition: To beat strongly and painfully, as a wound does.
entries.definitionCN: 像伤口那样强烈而带痛地跳动。

entries.definition: One complete cycle of the heart's pumping.
entries.definitionCN: 心脏泵血的一次完整周期。

entries.definition: A regular pattern of beats or movements.
entries.definitionCN: 节拍或动作的规律型式。

normalIntro.en: The word is Latin for a blow, and the whole family keeps that single strike repeated at a steady interval.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词在拉丁语里意为「一击」，整个词族都保留着同一记敲击按固定间隔反复出现的意思。

normal.en: Pulse is Latin pulsus, a beat, from pellere, to strike, so the word begins as a blow rather than as blood.
normal.cn: pulse 是拉丁 pulsus（一击），出自 pellere（击打），所以这个词起点是敲击而不是血。

normal.en: Pulsate adds -ate to the same stem: to keep striking, therefore to throb.
normal.cn: pulsate 在同一词干后加 -ate：不断敲击，因此是搏动。

normal.en: Impulse puts in- in front of pulsus: a push coming into you from outside.
normal.cn: impulse 在 pulsus 前加 in-：一股从外面推到你身上的力。

normal.en: Take someone's pulse is the oldest use, because the wrist is where the beating is easiest to feel.
normal.cn: take someone's pulse 是最老的用法，因为手腕上最容易摸到搏动。

normal.en: An electric pulse is one beat of a signal, with silence on either side, exactly like a single heartbeat.
normal.cn: 电脉冲是信号的一记跳动，两侧都是静默，和一次心跳完全一样。

abstract.en: A pulse is a rhythm you can prove with your fingertips, which is why the word suits both blood and music.
abstract.cn: 脉搏是一种可以用指尖证明的节奏，所以这个词既适合血液也适合音乐。

abstract.en: Everything alive here is described by what it does at intervals, not by what it is at rest.
abstract.cn: 这里凡是活着的东西，都用它隔一段时间就做一次的事来描述，而不是静止时的样子。

abstract.en: A city can have a pulse only because people agree to move at the same hours.
abstract.cn: 城市之所以有脉动，只因为人们同意在同一批时段里活动。

examples.en: Her pulse was fast but steady.
examples.cn: 她的脉搏很快，但很平稳。

examples.en: The sensor records every pulse of light.
examples.cn: 传感器记录每一束光脉冲。

examples.en: Drums pulsed somewhere behind the crowd.
examples.cn: 人群后方某处有鼓声一下下震动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「拍死」——手指按在腕上，那一下下拍到皮肤上的跳动，就是 pulse 脉搏。

root: 拉丁语 pellere（推动、击打）→ 过去分词 pulsus（一击、跳动）→ 古法语 pouls → 英语 pulse；核心是「按固定节奏的一记敲击」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one beat repeated at intervals; the senses divide into the heartbeat felt at the wrist, the single beat of a signal, the liveliness of a group, and the verb for throbbing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「按间隔反复出现的一记跳动」；义项由此分为腕上摸到的心跳、信号的一记脉冲、群体的活力，以及表示搏动的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two fingertips pressed to the inside of a wrist, a small regular knock rising through the skin.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根手指按在手腕内侧，皮肤下传上来一记记规律的轻敲。

branches.en: two fingers finding the beat under the skin
branches.cn: 两根手指在皮肤下找到那记跳动

branches.en: a single flash from a small device
branches.cn: 小装置发出的一次闪动

branches.en: a crowd whose noise rises and falls together
branches.cn: 喧声一起一落的人群

branches.en: drums shaking a wooden floor
branches.cn: 鼓声震动木地板

branches.en: the same rhythm inside a body and inside a street
branches.cn: 身体里与街道上同一种节律

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin verb for striking, its participle, the noun that came to English, and the English endings that build the verb and the noun of beating.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示击打的拉丁动词、它的过去分词、传入英语的名词，以及构成「搏动」动词与名词的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 呼吸；呼吸作用；一次呼吸；（生物的）气体交换
definition_en: the act or process of breathing, or in biology the exchange of gases between an organism and its environment and the release of energy from food
core_image: 胸腔一起一伏，空气从口鼻进入肺部，再带着二氧化碳出来
scene: 这里指「呼吸」。 Respiration slows during deep sleep as the body needs less oxygen.
sceneCN: 这里 respiration 指「呼吸动作」（第 1 个义项：吸进氧气、呼出二氧化碳的生理动作）；句意：深度睡眠时呼吸变慢，因为身体需要的氧气减少。图中可辨识物件：胸腔轮廓、肺、气流箭头、睡眠监测仪。

pos.zh: 呼吸；呼吸作用；一次呼吸；气体交换（指过程时不可数，指一次呼吸时可用复数 respirations）

senses.title: Breathing in and out
senses.titleCN: 呼吸动作：吸进与呼出
senses.definition: the physical act of drawing air into the lungs and letting it out again
senses.definitionCN: 把空气吸入肺再呼出的身体动作
senses.example: Respiration slows during deep sleep as the body needs less oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 深度睡眠时呼吸变慢，因为身体需要的氧气减少。
senses.why: Latin respirare meant 'to breathe again'; the noun starts as the repeated cycle of taking air and giving it back.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 respirare 意为「再次呼吸」；这个名词的起点是吸气与还气的反复循环。

senses.title: Gas exchange
senses.titleCN: 气体交换：氧气进入、二氧化碳排出
senses.definition: the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between blood and air in the lungs
senses.definitionCN: 血液与肺泡空气之间氧气与二氧化碳的交换
senses.example: External respiration takes place across the alveolar membrane.
senses.exampleCN: 外呼吸发生在肺泡膜两侧。
senses.why: Physiology separated the visible movement of the chest from the chemical exchange it serves.
senses.whyCN: 生理学把可见的胸廓运动与它所服务的化学交换区分开来。

senses.title: Cellular respiration
senses.titleCN: 细胞呼吸：细胞分解有机物释放能量
senses.definition: the chemical process in cells that releases energy from glucose, usually using oxygen
senses.definitionCN: 细胞内分解葡萄糖释放能量的化学过程，通常使用氧气
senses.example: Cellular respiration turns glucose into ATP and carbon dioxide.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞呼吸把葡萄糖变成 ATP 与二氧化碳。
senses.why: The same word scales down from the lungs to the mitochondrion, because both are exchanges of gases and energy.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从肺缩小到线粒体，因为两者都是气体与能量的交换。

senses.title: One breath
senses.titleCN: 一次呼吸：一吸一呼的计数单位
senses.definition: a single cycle of inhalation and exhalation, used as a countable unit
senses.definitionCN: 一次吸气与呼气的完整循环，作可数单位使用
senses.example: The patient takes about twelve respirations a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 这位病人每分钟大约呼吸十二次。
senses.why: The countable sense comes from counting cycles, the way heartbeat is counted.
senses.whyCN: 可数义来自对循环的计数，计数方式与心跳相同。

senses.title: Respiratory capacity
senses.titleCN: 呼吸功能：完成气体交换的能力
senses.definition: the ability of a person or organism to carry out breathing and gas exchange
senses.definitionCN: 人或生物完成呼吸与气体交换的能力
senses.example: Illness reduced her respiration and she needed oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 疾病削弱了她的呼吸功能，需要吸氧。
senses.why: As with many action nouns, the process can stand for the capacity to perform it.
senses.whyCN: 与许多动作名词一样，过程可以代指完成该过程的能力。

senses.title: Artificial respiration
senses.titleCN: 人工呼吸：替他人维持通气
senses.definition: the act of helping or replacing someone's breathing by machine or by mouth
senses.definitionCN: 用机器或口对口方式帮助或替代他人呼吸
senses.example: Artificial respiration kept him alive until the ambulance arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 人工呼吸让他撑到救护车到来。
senses.why: Emergency medicine turned the noun into a fixed phrase for a life-saving substitute action.
senses.whyCN: 急救医学把这个名词变成固定短语，指一种救命的替代动作。

senses.title: Plant respiration
senses.titleCN: 植物呼吸：植物同样吸氧放二氧化碳
senses.definition: in botany, the uptake of oxygen and release of carbon dioxide by plant cells, day and night
senses.definitionCN: 植物学中指植物细胞昼夜吸收氧气并释放二氧化碳
senses.example: Root respiration uses oxygen from the air spaces in soil.
senses.exampleCN: 根系呼吸使用土壤空隙中的氧气。
senses.why: Botany needed the term to correct the old belief that plants only produce oxygen.
senses.whyCN: 植物学需要这个词来纠正「植物只产氧」的旧看法。

senses.title: A living metaphor
senses.titleCN: 拟人用法：森林或城市的「呼吸」
senses.definition: figuratively, the visible rhythm of breathing attributed to a place or a large system
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，把呼吸的节律赋予一个地方或一个庞大系统
senses.example: You can feel the slow respiration of the forest at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时分，你能感到森林缓慢的呼吸。
senses.why: Writers lend the bodily rhythm to landscapes, because a forest also exchanges gases on a vast scale.
senses.whyCN: 作家把身体的节律借给风景，因为森林同样在巨大尺度上交换气体。

senses.title: Anaerobic respiration
senses.titleCN: 无氧呼吸：没有氧气也能释放能量
senses.definition: energy release from food without oxygen, producing lactate, ethanol or other products
senses.definitionCN: 无氧条件下从食物中释放能量，产生乳酸、乙醇等产物
senses.example: Anaerobic respiration in muscles produces lactate during a sprint.
senses.exampleCN: 短跑时肌肉的无氧呼吸产生乳酸。
senses.why: The word's core is exchange and energy release, so it can name a version that needs no external air at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是交换与能量释放，因此也能命名一种完全不需要外界空气的版本。

intro.en: Respiration comes from Latin respiratio, built on respirare 'to breathe again', from re- 'again' and spirare 'to breathe'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: respiration 出自拉丁 respiratio，由 respirare「再次呼吸」构成，而 respirare 来自 re-「再次」与 spirare「呼吸」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Spirare meant 'to breathe, to blow'. Its family is wide: spiritus 'breath, spirit', inspirare 'to breathe into', expirare 'to breathe out'.
items.cn: spirare 意为「呼吸、吹」。其词族很广：spiritus「气息、精神」、inspirare「吹入」、expirare「呼出」。

items.en: Respirare added re- 'again' or 'back': to breathe again, to recover breath, to take a rest. Classical Latin used it for catching one's breath after effort.
items.cn: respirare 加 re-「再次、返回」：再次呼吸、缓过气来、休息。古典拉丁用它指用力之后喘过气来。

items.en: Respiratio named the act of breathing again and, by extension, the ordinary process of breathing.
items.cn: respiratio 指再次呼吸的动作，并引申为一般的呼吸过程。

items.en: English respiration is recorded in the fourteenth century, at first as a general word for breathing and for rest after exertion.
items.cn: 英语 respiration 记录于 14 世纪，起初泛指呼吸以及用力后的歇息。

items.en: From the seventeenth century onward physiology split the word into external respiration in the lungs and internal or cellular respiration in the tissues.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起，生理学把这个词分为肺内的外呼吸与组织内的内呼吸或细胞呼吸。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation is uncertain, and the deeper Indo-European root behind spirare is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与更深词根）：英语最早书证年代存疑；spirare 背后的更深印欧词根属重构形式，并非有记录的实际词。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same Latin family that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for breathing and gas exchange.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族、容易混淆的词；第二组是「呼吸与气体交换」的近义词。

entries.definition: To breathe; the verb names the action, while respiration names the process or one cycle of it.
entries.definitionCN: 呼吸；动词指动作，respiration 指过程或其中的一次循环。

entries.definition: Relating to breathing, as in respiratory system; it describes organs and functions rather than the act.
entries.definitionCN: 与呼吸有关，如呼吸系统；它描述器官与功能，而非动作。

entries.definition: A mask or machine that supplies air or filters it; it is a countable object, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 供气或滤气的面罩或机器；是可数物件，不是过程。

entries.definition: Sweating through the skin; it shares the Latin spirare root but names water loss, not gas exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 经皮肤出汗；它与 respiration 共享拉丁 spirare 词根，但指失水，而非气体交换。

entries.definition: The ordinary English word for moving air in and out; respiration is the technical and biological term.
entries.definitionCN: 日常英语中「吸进呼出空气」的普通词；respiration 是技术与生物学用语。

entries.definition: The mechanical movement of air into and out of the lungs; it names the transport, while respiration includes the exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 空气进出肺的机械运动；它命名输送，而 respiration 还包括交换。

entries.definition: The transfer of oxygen and carbon dioxide across a membrane; it is the functional core of respiration.
entries.definitionCN: 氧气与二氧化碳跨膜转移，是呼吸的功能核心。

entries.definition: All the chemical reactions of a living body; cellular respiration is one part of metabolism.
entries.definitionCN: 生物体全部的化学反应；细胞呼吸只是代谢的一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'again' + spirare 'breathe': breathing is a cycle that repeats.
normal.cn: re-「再次」+ spirare「呼吸」：呼吸是不断重复的循环。

normal.en: The family runs respire, respiratory, respirator, respirometer and respiration.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 respire、respiratory、respirator、respirometer、respiration。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the science: cellular respiration, aerobic respiration, artificial respiration, external respiration.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出科学语境：细胞呼吸、有氧呼吸、人工呼吸、外呼吸。

normal.en: spirare also gives spirit, inspire, expire and conspire.
normal.cn: spirare 还衍生出 spirit、inspire、expire、conspire。

normal.en: Breathing is ventilation; the chemistry it enables is respiration.
normal.cn: 呼吸动作是 ventilation，它促成的化学过程才是 respiration。

abstract.en: Picture a tide going in and out of a chest, slow and even.
abstract.cn: 想象潮水在胸腔里进出，缓慢而均匀。

abstract.en: Picture a mitochondrion as a tiny furnace that takes sugar and oxygen and gives out energy.
abstract.cn: 想象线粒体是一座小炉子，吃进糖与氧，放出能量。

abstract.en: Picture a forest at dawn, mist moving as if the whole wood were breathing.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时的森林，雾气流动，仿佛整片树林在呼吸。

examples.en: Respiration rate is one of the vital signs recorded on admission.
examples.cn: 呼吸频率是入院时记录的生命体征之一。

examples.en: Cellular respiration releases energy stored in glucose.
examples.cn: 细胞呼吸释放储存在葡萄糖中的能量。

examples.en: Anaerobic respiration allows muscles to work without enough oxygen.
examples.cn: 无氧呼吸让肌肉在氧气不足时仍能工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re 再次 + spir 呼吸 + ation 过程」——一遍遍再呼吸 → respiration 呼吸

root: 拉丁 re-「再次」+ spirare「呼吸」→ respirare「再次呼吸、缓气」→ respiratio「呼吸」→ 英语 respiration。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one cycle: air goes in and out, the body takes oxygen and gives back carbon dioxide, and that exchange can happen in a lung, a cell, a plant or a whole forest.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个循环展开：空气进出，身体取氧还碳，而这种交换可以发生在肺里、细胞里、植物里，也可以发生在一整片森林里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: air moving in and out of a body, taking oxygen and returning carbon dioxide.
core.cn: 核心意象：空气进出身体，取走氧气，还回二氧化碳。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE CYCLE: the chest movement and the single counted breath are the same event at two scales.
branches.cn: 可见的循环：胸廓运动与可计数的单次呼吸，是同一事件的两个尺度。

branches.en: THE CHEMISTRY: gas exchange can run with oxygen or without it, in lungs or in muscle.
branches.cn: 化学层面：气体交换可以在有氧或无氧、在肺里或肌肉里进行。

branches.en: THE CELL: the same word names the mitochondrial breakdown of glucose.
branches.cn: 细胞一端：同一个词也命名线粒体对葡萄糖的分解。

branches.en: CAPACITY AND SUBSTITUTE: the process becomes an ability, and medicine can replace it artificially.
branches.cn: 能力与替代：过程变成能力，医学也能用人工方式替代它。

branches.en: BEYOND ANIMALS: plants respire too, and writers lend the rhythm to whole landscapes.
branches.cn: 动物之外：植物也会呼吸，作家则把这个节律借给整片风景。

intro.en: Respiration is a Latin verb of breathing plus a noun of action: re- + spirare + -tio.
intro.cn: respiration 是拉丁「呼吸」动词加动作名词后缀：re- + spirare + -tio。

latinIntro.en: Latin spirare 'to breathe' supplies spirit, inspire, expire, conspire and respirare; respiratio gives English respiration, respire and respiratory.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 spirare「呼吸」衍生出 spirit、inspire、expire、conspire、respirare；respiratio 给出英语 respiration、respire、respiratory。

items.example: The respiratory tract runs from nose to lungs.

items.meaning: a device that supplies or filters air

items.example: The respirometer tracked oxygen uptake in the soil.
items.exampleCN: 呼吸测量仪追踪了土壤的耗氧量。

items.example: The word spirit began as a word for breath.
items.exampleCN: spirit 最初是表示呼吸的词。

items.meaning: to breathe life into; to stimulate
to breathe out; to come to an end

latinEntries.meaning: to breathe again, to recover breath
a breathing; a recovery of breath

definition_zh: 新陈代谢；生物体内全部化学变化的总和；物质与能量的转化
definition_en: the whole set of chemical reactions by which a living organism converts substances and energy, keeping itself running
core_image: 一条环形的流水线在同一个身体里转圈，一端拆开原料，另一端拼出新件，中间不断放热
scene: 这里指「新陈代谢」。 A hibernating animal slows its metabolism so that one stored fat reserve lasts the whole winter.
sceneCN: 这里 metabolism 指「代谢整体、代谢速率」（第 1 个义项：体内全部化学变化的总和及其运行强度）；冬眠动物让它放慢，一份脂肪储备就能撑过整个冬天。图中可辨识物件：环形流水线、拆解的原料、拼出的新件、散出的热。

pos.zh: 新陈代谢；代谢（不可数；指不同生物或不同个体的代谢体系时可用复数 metabolisms）

senses.title: The whole chemical turnover
senses.titleCN: 新陈代谢：体内全部化学变化的总和
senses.definition: the entire set of chemical reactions that keep an organism alive
senses.definitionCN: 维持生物体存活所需的全部化学反应
senses.example: Metabolism includes both the burning of fuel and the building of new tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 新陈代谢既包括燃烧燃料，也包括构建新组织。
senses.why: Greek metabolē meant 'a change, a turning over'; physiology took the word for the constant change inside a body, so the name starts as change itself.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 metabolē 意为「变化、翻转」；生理学用它指体内持续发生的更换，因此这个名字的起点就是「变化」。

senses.title: Materials passing through
senses.titleCN: 物质代谢：原料的进出与转化
senses.definition: the material side of that turnover, the conversion of substances into other substances
senses.definitionCN: 这一周转的物质面：一种物质被转化为另一种物质
senses.example: Protein metabolism decides how much nitrogen the body keeps.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋白质代谢决定身体保留多少氮。
senses.why: because the change is chemical, the word also names the material side of the turnover, not only its energy side.
senses.whyCN: 由于变化是化学性的，这个词也命名周转的物质面，而不只是能量面。

senses.title: Energy in and out
senses.titleCN: 能量代谢：放热与耗能
senses.definition: the energy side of the turnover, the release of energy from fuel and its use for work
senses.definitionCN: 周转的能量面：从燃料释放能量并用于做功
senses.example: Energy metabolism converts food into heat and movement.
senses.exampleCN: 能量代谢把食物转化为热与运动。
senses.why: the same loop can be read as a budget of energy, so the word covers calories as well as molecules.
senses.whyCN: 同一条环路也可以读成能量预算，因此这个词同时覆盖分子与卡路里。

senses.title: The idle rate
senses.titleCN: 基础代谢：静息时的最低消耗
senses.definition: the rate of turnover while at rest, measured as basal metabolism
senses.definitionCN: 静息状态下的周转速率，即基础代谢
senses.example: Basal metabolism accounts for most of the calories a sedentary adult burns.
senses.exampleCN: 基础代谢占久坐成年人消耗热量的绝大部分。
senses.why: once measured in the clinic, the word also names a rate, the speed of the loop rather than its contents.
senses.whyCN: 当它在临床被测定后，这个词也命名一个速率，即环路的快慢而非内容。

senses.title: The tearing-down half
senses.titleCN: 分解代谢：拆开与放能
senses.definition: the breaking-down half of the turnover, catabolism, which releases energy
senses.definitionCN: 周转中拆解并释放能量的那一半，即分解代谢
senses.example: Catabolism breaks glucose into carbon dioxide and water.
senses.exampleCN: 分解代谢把葡萄糖拆成二氧化碳和水。
senses.why: the loop has two halves, and the tearing side is one of them; the word as a whole can name that half.
senses.whyCN: 环路有两半，拆解的一侧是其中之一；作为一个整体，这个词也可指那一半。

senses.title: The building half
senses.titleCN: 合成代谢：拼装与耗能
senses.definition: the building half of the turnover, anabolism, which consumes energy
senses.definitionCN: 周转中拼装并消耗能量的那一半，即合成代谢
senses.example: Anabolism uses ATP to assemble amino acids into muscle.
senses.exampleCN: 合成代谢用 ATP 把氨基酸组装成肌肉。
senses.why: because the same loop both breaks and builds, the whole word can stand for the constructing half as well.
senses.whyCN: 由于同一条环路既拆又建，整个词也可指构建的那一半。

senses.title: What the body does to a drug
senses.titleCN: 药物代谢：体内对药物的改造
senses.definition: the chemical alteration of drugs and other foreign compounds inside the body
senses.definitionCN: 药物及其他外来化合物在体内被化学改造的过程
senses.example: A fast metabolism clears the drug before the next dose is due.
senses.exampleCN: 代谢快的人在下一次给药前就把药清除掉了。
senses.why: pharmacology applies the loop to foreign molecules, so the word also names detoxification rather than nourishment.
senses.whyCN: 药理学把这条环路用于外来分子，因此这个词也命名解毒过程，而不是营养过程。

senses.title: The map of all routes
senses.titleCN: 代谢网络：全部通路的集合
senses.definition: the network of all the pathways taken together, studied as a system
senses.definitionCN: 把全部通路作为一个系统来研究的网络
senses.example: Systems biology draws the whole metabolism as a map of arrows.
senses.exampleCN: 系统生物学把整个代谢画成一张箭头地图。
senses.why: when the single loop is scaled up, it becomes a network; the singular word then names the map rather than a reaction.
senses.whyCN: 当单一环路被放大，它就成了网络；单数形式此时命名的是那张地图，而不是某一反应。

intro.en: Metabolism comes from Greek metabolē 'a change, a turning over', built on meta- 'over, beyond' and ballein 'to throw'. English first used it for change in general.
intro.cn: metabolism 出自希腊 metabolē「变化、翻转」，由 meta-「越过」与 ballein「投掷」构成。英语最初用它泛指变化。

items.en: metabolē named a change or a turning over, including a change of government. The base is a Greek noun of action, not a Latin one.
items.cn: metabolē 指变化或翻转，也包括政权的更替。其词基是希腊动作名词，不是拉丁语。

items.en: ballein 'to throw' supplies the second element; meta- adds the idea of change of place or state. The deeper origin of ballein is not settled.
items.cn: ballein「投掷」提供第二个构件；meta- 加入位置或状态改变的意思。ballein 的更深来源并无定论。

items.en: English metabolism appears in the seventeenth century for change in general; the first citation is approximate.
items.cn: 英语 metabolism 于 17 世纪出现，泛指变化；最早书证年代为约数。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physiology narrowed the word to the chemical turnover of a living body, the sense that now dominates.
items.cn: 19 世纪生理学把该词收窄为活体内的化学周转，即今天主导的义项。

items.en: Twentieth-century biochemistry split the loop into catabolism and anabolism and mapped the pathways as a network.
items.cn: 20 世纪生物化学把环路分成分解代谢与合成代谢，并把它绘成通路网络。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): ballein has no agreed pre-Greek source, so any Indo-European form behind it is a reconstruction; the earliest English date is also approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ballein 在希腊语之前的来源并无共识，其背后的印欧形式属重构；英语最早书证年代亦为约数。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes that share meta- but not always the same root; group two holds the two halves and the neighbouring processes.
note.cn: 第一组是共享 meta- 但未必同源的形近词；第二组是这一过程的两半以及相邻过程。

entries.definition: The adjective 'of metabolism'; it qualifies rate, pathway or disease but does not name the whole turnover.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「代谢的」；修饰速率、通路或疾病，但不命名整个周转过程。

entries.definition: The spread of cancer, from Greek meta- 'beyond' plus stasis 'standing'. It shares the prefix and not the root, so it is not a relative of metabolism.
entries.definitionCN: 指癌症的转移，由希腊 meta-「越过」加 stasis「站立」构成；只共享前缀而词根不同，因此与 metabolism 并非同族。

entries.definition: A substance produced or consumed during metabolism; it is an item in the loop, not the loop.
entries.definitionCN: 指代谢过程中产生或消耗的物质；是环路中的一项，而不是环路。

entries.definition: A figure of speech, from meta- 'over' plus pherein 'to carry'. Another meta- word with an unrelated root.
entries.definitionCN: 一种修辞，由 meta-「越过」加 pherein「搬运」构成；又一个前缀相同而词根无关的词。

entries.definition: The set of reactions that break molecules down and release energy; it is one half of metabolism.
entries.definitionCN: 指拆解分子并释放能量的一组反应；是代谢的一半。

entries.definition: The set of reactions that build molecules and consume energy; the other half of metabolism.
entries.definitionCN: 指构建分子并消耗能量的一组反应；是代谢的另一半。

entries.definition: The process by which cells obtain energy from fuel, usually with oxygen; it is a major route inside metabolism.
entries.definitionCN: 指细胞从燃料获取能量、通常需氧的过程；是代谢内部的主干路线。

entries.definition: The breakdown of food before it enters the body's chemistry; digestion precedes most metabolism.
entries.definitionCN: 指食物进入体内化学之前的分解；消化先于大部分代谢。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: meta- 'over' + ballein 'to throw': a constant throwing over, change itself.
normal.cn: meta-「越过」+ ballein「投掷」：不停翻来覆去地更换，也就是「变化」本身。

normal.en: The family runs metabolism, metabolic, metabolize, metabolite, metabolomics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 metabolism、metabolic、metabolize、metabolite、metabolomics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: basal metabolism, energy metabolism, lipid metabolism, drug metabolism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：基础代谢、能量代谢、脂质代谢、药物代谢。

normal.en: The loop has two halves: catabolism tears down, anabolism builds up.
normal.cn: 环路有两半：分解代谢拆，合成代谢建。

normal.en: A slow metabolism is a rate, not a substance; do not confuse it with a metabolite.
normal.cn: 「代谢慢」说的是速率，不是物质；别与代谢产物混为一谈。

abstract.en: Picture a loop of conveyor belts that never stop, tearing and joining at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一条不停的环形传送带，一边拆一边接。

abstract.en: Picture a stove that both burns wood and builds furniture from the same pile.
abstract.cn: 想象一座炉子，同一堆木料既用来烧，也用来做家具。

abstract.en: Picture an accounting book where income and spending are kept in one column.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账，收入与支出记在同一栏里。

examples.en: Regular exercise raises resting metabolism for several hours.
examples.cn: 规律运动会提高数小时的静息代谢。

examples.en: The liver handles most drug metabolism in the body.
examples.cn: 体内大部分药物代谢由肝脏承担。

examples.en: Metabolism in a dormant seed nearly stops until water returns.
examples.cn: 休眠种子在水分回来之前代谢几乎停止。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「每天（meta）都在烧（bal）」——身体里不停拆与建的化学周转 → 新陈代谢

root: 希腊 metabolē「变化、翻转」（meta-「越过」+ ballein「投掷」）→ 英语 metabolism；19 世纪收窄为体内化学周转。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a loop keeps turning inside a body, and that turning is read as the whole turnover, as materials, as energy, as a resting rate, as the tearing half, as the building half, as drug clearing, and as a map of all routes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：身体里的一条环路不停转动，这次转动依次被读成整体周转、物质、能量、静息速率、拆解的一半、构建的一半、药物清除，以及全部路线的地图。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed loop that tears materials apart at one end and joins new ones at the other, shedding heat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条闭环，一端拆开材料，另一端拼出新物，同时散出热。

branches.en: THE WHOLE LOOP: the turnover as such, the plainest sense.
branches.cn: 整条环路：周转本身，最朴素的义项。

branches.en: TWO LEDGERS: the same loop read as material flow and as energy flow.
branches.cn: 两本账：同一条环路被读成物质流与能量流。

branches.en: SPEED: at rest the loop has a measurable idle rate.
branches.cn: 速度：静息时环路有一个可测的怠速。

branches.en: TWO HALVES: tearing down and building up, each able to stand for the whole.
branches.cn: 两半：拆解与构建，各自都能代指整体。

branches.en: FOREIGN MATTER AND MAP: clearing drugs, and drawing every route as one network.
branches.cn: 外来物与地图：清除药物，并把所有路线绘成一张网络。

intro.en: Metabolism is a Greek compound behind a Latinized ending -ismus; the English family adds Latin -ic and -ita and Greek -omics.
intro.cn: metabolism 是拉丁化词尾 -ismus 包裹的希腊合成词；英语词族另加拉丁 -ic、-ita 与希腊 -omics。

latinIntro.en: No inherited Latin base exists. New Latin metabolismus is a Latinized spelling; the -ismus ending reached English through Latin and French.
latinIntro.cn: 没有传承的拉丁词基。新拉丁语 metabolismus 是拉丁化拼写；-ismus 词尾经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

items.meaning: the turnover of a living body
to subject a substance to metabolism
a substance made or used in metabolism
items.meaningCN: 代谢中生成或消耗的物质
items.example: Lactate is a metabolite of glucose.
items.exampleCN: 乳酸是葡萄糖的一种代谢产物。

items.example: Metabolomics compares hundreds of small molecules.
items.exampleCN: 代谢组学比较数百种小分子。
分解代谢从脂肪中释放能量。

items.example: Anabolism requires energy and building blocks.
items.exampleCN: 合成代谢需要能量与构建单元。

items.meaning: a person or organ that metabolizes
items.exampleCN: 快代谢型的人清除咖啡因很快。

items.example: Basal metabolism is measured after sleep.
items.exampleCN: 基础代谢在睡眠后测定。

latinEntries.structure: basis, basis (f., Greek loanword, third declension)

definition_zh: 消化；消化过程；（对信息或经历的）消化吸收
definition_en: the process by which food is broken down into substances the body can absorb, or the mental process of absorbing information
core_image: 一块食物在消化道里被逐步拆小、溶开，最后变成可被吸收的细小分子
scene: 这里指「消化」。 Chewing slowly aids digestion by giving enzymes more time to act.
sceneCN: 这里 digestion 指「消化过程」（第 3 个义项：食物在消化道中被机械与化学作用分解的全过程）；句意：细嚼慢咽有助于消化，因为酶有更多时间起作用。图中可辨识物件：牙齿、食管、胃、小肠、消化酶示意。

pos.zh: 消化；消化过程；消化能力；（对信息、经历的）消化吸收（不可数，指具体一次消化时用复数 digestions）

senses.title: Mechanical breakdown
senses.titleCN: 机械消化：咀嚼与蠕动把食物弄碎
senses.definition: the physical part of digestion, in which teeth crush food and the gut wall churns it
senses.definitionCN: 消化中的物理部分，牙齿把食物压碎、肠壁把它搅动
senses.example: Mechanical digestion begins the moment you bite into an apple.
senses.exampleCN: 你咬下苹果的那一刻，机械消化就开始了。
senses.why: Latin digerere meant 'to separate, to carry apart'; the first step of that separating is simply breaking a mass into smaller pieces.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 digerere 意为「分开、搬运开来」；这种分开的第一步，就是把一整块弄成更小的块。

senses.title: Chemical breakdown
senses.titleCN: 化学消化：酸与酶把食物分解成分子
senses.definition: the chemical part of digestion, in which acid and enzymes split large molecules into absorbable ones
senses.definitionCN: 消化中的化学部分，酸与酶把大分子拆成可吸收的小分子
senses.example: Chemical digestion of protein starts in the stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋白质的化学消化从胃里开始。
senses.why: Once chemists identified enzymes, the 'separating' action could be described as a chemical splitting rather than a physical one.
senses.whyCN: 化学家识别出酶之后，「分开」这一动作便可描述为化学拆分，而非物理弄碎。

senses.title: The whole digestive process
senses.titleCN: 消化过程：从入口到吸收的整条流程
senses.definition: the complete sequence from chewing to absorption, taken as one process
senses.definitionCN: 从咀嚼到吸收的完整序列，作为一个整体过程来看
senses.example: Chewing slowly aids digestion by giving enzymes more time to act.
senses.exampleCN: 细嚼慢咽有助于消化，因为酶有更多时间起作用。
senses.why: The noun of action naturally names the whole event, not just one stage inside it.
senses.whyCN: 动作名词天然指整个事件，而不只是其中的某个阶段。

senses.title: Digestive capacity
senses.titleCN: 消化能力：一个人能处理好食物的程度
senses.definition: a person's or an animal's ability to deal with a particular food without discomfort
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物处理某种食物而不感到不适的能力
senses.example: Rich sauces are beyond my digestion.
senses.exampleCN: 油腻的酱汁我的肠胃消化不了。
senses.why: The process came to stand for the capacity to carry it out, a common shift from action to ability.
senses.whyCN: 过程转而代表完成该过程的能力，这是「动作转能力」的常见引申。

senses.title: Absorption after breakdown
senses.titleCN: 消化吸收：分解之后的养分进入体内
senses.definition: the outcome of digestion, namely nutrients passing through the gut wall into the blood
senses.definitionCN: 消化的结果，即养分穿过肠壁进入血液
senses.example: Poor digestion limits how much iron the body actually gets.
senses.exampleCN: 消化不佳会限制身体实际获得的铁量。
senses.why: In nutrition writing the word often includes the absorption that follows, because the two are measured together.
senses.whyCN: 在营养学写作中，这个词常把随后的吸收也算进来，因为两者是一起测量的。

senses.title: Anaerobic digestion
senses.titleCN: 厌氧消化：微生物在无氧条件下分解有机物
senses.definition: in waste treatment, the breakdown of organic matter by microorganisms without oxygen, producing biogas
senses.definitionCN: 在废物处理中，微生物在无氧条件下分解有机物并产生沼气
senses.example: The plant turns food waste into gas through anaerobic digestion.
senses.exampleCN: 该厂通过厌氧消化把厨余变成燃气。
senses.why: Engineers borrowed the bodily word for an industrial version of the same breaking-down of organic matter.
senses.whyCN: 工程师借用了身体里的词，指工业上对有机物进行的同类分解。

senses.title: Mental assimilation
senses.titleCN: 信息消化：把读到的内容变成自己的理解
senses.definition: the process of understanding and absorbing ideas, news or a book over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间推移理解并吸收观点、消息或一本书的过程
senses.example: The report needs a week of digestion before we act on it.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告需要我们消化一周，再据此行动。
senses.why: The metaphor is old: ideas are food that must be broken down before they can nourish thought.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻很古老：观点是食物，必须先被分解，才能滋养思想。

senses.title: Digestion time
senses.titleCN: 消化时间：食物在体内停留多久
senses.definition: the period a meal takes to move through the stomach and gut
senses.definitionCN: 一餐食物通过胃与肠道所需的时间
senses.example: Fat slows digestion, which is why a heavy lunch keeps you full.
senses.exampleCN: 脂肪会延长消化时间，所以一顿油腻的午餐让人久饱。
senses.why: Time is the measurable face of the process, so the noun often stands for its duration.
senses.whyCN: 时间是这一过程可测量的一面，因此这个名词常直接表示其时长。

senses.title: Settling an experience
senses.titleCN: 慢慢消化：让经历或情绪沉淀下来
senses.definition: figuratively, the slow working-through of an event or feeling before it can be accepted
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指慢慢消化一件事或一种情绪，直到能够接受
senses.example: She needs time for the digestion of the bad news.
senses.exampleCN: 她需要时间消化这个坏消息。
senses.why: The bodily image extends to emotion: what is hard to take in must first be broken down internally.
senses.whyCN: 身体的意象延伸到情绪：难以接受的事，必须先在心里被拆解。

intro.en: Digestion comes from Latin digestio, built on digerere 'to carry apart, to distribute'. Its oldest sense was not about the stomach at all. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: digestion 出自拉丁 digestio，由 digerere「分开搬运、分配」构成。它最早的义项与胃并无关系。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Digerere combined dis- 'apart' with gerere 'to carry, to conduct'. It meant to separate things and carry them to their places, as an army or a household is arranged.
items.cn: digerere 由 dis-「分开」与 gerere「搬运、进行」合成，意为把事物分开并各归其位，如同安排一支军队或一个家庭。

items.en: Digestio named an arranging or distribution. Classical Latin could speak of the digestio of a meal in the sense of its being distributed through the body, not of its being dissolved in the stomach.
items.cn: digestio 指安排或分配。古典拉丁可说一顿饭的 digestio，意思是它被分配输送到全身，而不是在胃里被溶解。

items.en: Medical writers narrowed the word to the processing of food inside the body, and the older sense of orderly distribution faded.
items.cn: 医学作者把词义收窄为食物在体内的加工过程，原先「有序分配」的旧义逐渐消失。

items.en: English digestion is recorded in the fourteenth century, through Old French, already with the bodily sense alongside the general one of arranging.
items.cn: 英语 digestion 于 14 世纪经由古法语出现，已带有身体义，同时保留「安排」的一般义。

items.en: Chemistry and engineering later added chemical digestion and anaerobic digestion; the mental sense, though old as a metaphor, became common in modern writing about information.
items.cn: 化学与工程后来加入化学消化与厌氧消化；心理义虽是古老比喻，却在现代关于信息的写作中变得常见。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation is uncertain, and the semantic path from 'distribution' to 'food processing' is inferred rather than documented step by step.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与语义路径）：英语最早书证年代存疑；从「分配」到「食物加工」的语义路径属推断，并无逐步记录。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same Latin family that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for breaking food or ideas down.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族、容易混淆的词；第二组是「把食物或观点拆解」的近义词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to break food down or to absorb information; as a noun it means a summary, a different line from Latin digesta.
entries.definitionCN: 动词指分解食物或吸收信息；作名词则指摘要，这条线出自拉丁 digesta，与动词义不同。

entries.definition: Means 'relating to digestion', and describes organs, juices or biscuits rather than the process itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「消化的」，形容器官、消化液或消化饼干，而不是过程本身。

entries.definition: Means 'able to be digested', a property of food; it does not name the process.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「可消化的」，是食物的属性，不指过程。

entries.definition: Pain or discomfort from food that is not being digested well; the in- prefix reverses the healthy process.
entries.definitionCN: 食物消化不顺带来的疼痛或不适；in- 前缀把健康的消化过程反转过来。

entries.definition: The body's use of absorbed nutrients; it follows digestion rather than replacing it.
entries.definitionCN: 身体对已吸收养分的利用，发生在消化之后，并不取代消化。

entries.definition: The passage of nutrients through the gut wall into blood; digestion breaks food down, absorption moves it in.
entries.definitionCN: 养分穿过肠壁进入血液的过程；digestion 负责拆解，absorption 负责送入。

entries.definition: All the chemical reactions that use and store nutrients; it begins where digestion ends.
entries.definitionCN: 利用与储存养分的全部化学反应，起点正是消化的终点。

entries.definition: A general word for something splitting into parts; it can describe machines or arguments as well as food.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某物分裂成部分，既可指食物，也可指机器或论证。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: dis- 'apart' + gerere 'carry': food is carried apart into pieces.
normal.cn: dis-「分开」+ gerere「搬运」：食物被分开、被搬运成小块。

normal.en: The family runs digest, digestive, digestible, indigestion and digestibility.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 digest、digestive、digestible、indigestion、digestibility。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: aid digestion, slow digestion, anaerobic digestion, digestion time.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出场景：帮助消化、消化缓慢、厌氧消化、消化时间。

normal.en: Physiology separates mechanical digestion from chemical digestion.
normal.cn: 生理学把机械消化与化学消化分开。

normal.en: digestion breaks food down; absorption moves it in; metabolism uses it.
normal.cn: digestion 拆解食物，absorption 送进体内，metabolism 加以利用。

abstract.en: Picture a long river in which a lump of food is worn smaller and smaller until it dissolves.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长河，一块食物在其中被磨得越来越小，直至溶解。

abstract.en: Picture a book being cut into chapters, then notes, then ideas you can keep.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书被裁成章节，再变成笔记，最后变成你能留住的观点。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed tank where bacteria eat waste in the dark and release gas.
abstract.cn: 想象一个密闭罐，细菌在黑暗中吃掉废物并放出气体。

examples.en: Digestion of starch begins in the mouth, where saliva contains amylase.
examples.cn: 淀粉的消化从口腔开始，因为唾液中含有淀粉酶。

examples.en: A high-fibre meal slows digestion and steadies blood sugar.
examples.cn: 高纤维的一餐会减慢消化，并使血糖更平稳。

examples.en: The committee's digestion of the proposal took three meetings.
examples.cn: 委员会消化这份提案用了三次会议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「di 分开 + gest 搬运 + ion 过程」——把食物分开搬进身体 → digestion 消化

root: 拉丁 dis-「分开」+ gerere「搬运」→ digerere「分开搬走、分配」→ digestio「分配；消化」→ 英语 digestion。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one movement: a mass is separated into smaller parts, and that separating can be physical, chemical, industrial, or purely mental.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个动作展开：一整块被分开成更小的部分，而这种分开可以是物理的、化学的、工业的，也可以纯粹是心智上的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lump of food being carried apart into pieces small enough to pass through a wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块食物被分开搬走，直到小得能穿过一道壁。

branches.en: TWO HANDS OF THE SAME JOB: teeth and gut wall do the mechanical half, acid and enzymes do the chemical half.
branches.cn: 同一件活的两只手：牙齿与肠壁完成机械的一半，酸与酶完成化学的一半。

branches.en: THE WHOLE ARC AND ITS CLOCK: the process can be named as a single sequence, and also as the time that sequence takes.
branches.cn: 整条弧线与它的时钟：这个过程既可被命名为一个完整序列，也可被命名为它所耗费的时间。

branches.en: CAPACITY AND RESULT: the act becomes an ability, and the ability is judged by how much nutrient actually gets through.
branches.cn: 能力与结果：动作变成能力，而能力由实际有多少养分进入体内来评判。

branches.en: THE INDUSTRIAL COPY: bacteria in a tank perform the same breakdown without oxygen and produce fuel.
branches.cn: 工业复制：罐中的细菌在无氧条件下完成同样的分解，并产出燃料。

branches.en: THE MIND'S STOMACH: reports and bad news must also be broken down before they can be accepted.
branches.cn: 心智的胃：报告与坏消息同样要先被拆解，才能被接受。

intro.en: Digestion is a Latin verb of carrying apart plus a noun of action: dis- + gerere + -tio.
intro.cn: digestion 是拉丁「分开搬运」动词加动作名词后缀：dis- + gerere + -tio。

latinIntro.en: Latin digerere 'to carry apart' yields digestio, digestus and the English verb digest; the noun digest 'summary' comes instead from digesta, 'things arranged'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 digerere「分开搬运」衍生出 digestio、digestus 与英语动词 digest；名词 digest「摘要」则出自 digesta「被整理的事物」。

items.meaning: a carrying apart; the processing of food
items.meaningCN: 分开搬运；食物的加工过程
items.example: Digestion takes several hours for a fatty meal.
items.exampleCN: 一顿高脂餐的消化需要几个小时。

items.meaning: to break down food; to take in ideas

items.example: The digestive tract runs from mouth to anus.
items.exampleCN: 消化道从口腔延伸到肛门。

items.example: Cooked starch is more digestible than raw starch.
items.exampleCN: 熟淀粉比生淀粉更易消化。
纤维素对人体来说无法消化。

items.example: He took an antacid for indigestion.
items.exampleCN: 他吃了抗酸药缓解消化不良。

items.meaning: the degree to which food can be digested
items.example: Cooking raises the digestibility of protein.
items.exampleCN: 烹调会提高蛋白质的可消化性。

items.meaning: a drink taken after a meal to aid digestion
items.example: They served a herbal digestif after dinner.
items.exampleCN: 晚餐后他们上了一杯草本餐后酒。

latinEntries.meaning: to separate, to carry apart, to distribute
a distribution; the processing of food

definition_zh: 营养；营养学
definition_en: the process by which living things obtain and use the food they need, and the scientific study of that process
core_image: 一只餐盘被分成几块，旁边一本翻开的教科书与一条向上生长的曲线

pos.zh: 营养；营养学（多作不可数名词；指学科时为不可数）

senses.title: The process of being nourished
senses.titleCN: 营养过程：摄入与利用食物的全过程
senses.definition: the whole process by which an organism takes in food and uses it for energy, growth and repair
senses.definitionCN: 生物摄入食物并把它用于能量、生长与修复的全过程
senses.example: Nutrition begins with chewing and ends inside every cell.
senses.exampleCN: 营养从咀嚼开始，到每个细胞为止。
senses.why: The Latin action noun names an activity, not a substance, so nutrition is first of all something that happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动作名词命名的是活动而非物质，因此 nutrition 首先是一件正在发生的事。

senses.title: The scientific discipline
senses.titleCN: 营养学：研究食物与健康的学科
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies nutrients, how the body uses them and how diet affects health
senses.definitionCN: 研究养分、身体如何利用它们以及膳食如何影响健康的科学分支
senses.example: She studied nutrition before working in public health.
senses.exampleCN: 她在进入公共卫生领域之前学的是营养学。
senses.why: Because the process is complex enough to study, the same noun came to name the academic field without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 由于这一过程复杂到值得研究，同一个名词不需变形就成了一门学科的名字。

senses.title: The quality of a diet
senses.titleCN: 膳食质量：一个人实际获得的营养
senses.definition: the nourishment a person or population actually receives through their diet, judged as good or poor
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体通过膳食实际获得的营养，可评为良好或不足
senses.example: Good nutrition in early childhood pays off for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 幼儿期良好的营养会在几十年后仍然受益。
senses.why: Clinicians and policy makers speak of nutrition as a state to be assessed, so the process word also names a condition.
senses.whyCN: 临床医生与政策制定者把营养当作可评估的状态，因此过程词也指一种状况。

senses.title: Clinical nutrition
senses.titleCN: 临床营养：以营养手段治疗患者
senses.definition: the medical specialty that manages diet, tube feeding and intravenous feeding in illness
senses.definitionCN: 在疾病中管理膳食、管饲与静脉营养的医学专科
senses.example: The clinical nutrition team adjusted his tube feed.
senses.exampleCN: 临床营养团队调整了他的管饲配方。
senses.why: When eating is impossible, nutrition becomes a medical intervention with doses and protocols.
senses.whyCN: 当无法进食时，营养就变成有剂量与规程的医疗干预。

senses.title: Plant nutrition
senses.titleCN: 植物营养：根系吸收与光合作用
senses.definition: in botany, the way plants obtain mineral ions from soil and carbon from the air
senses.definitionCN: 植物学中指植物从土壤取得矿质离子、从空气取得碳的方式
senses.example: Plant nutrition depends on both root uptake and photosynthesis.
senses.exampleCN: 植物营养同时依赖根系吸收与光合作用。
senses.why: Botanists reuse the word for a completely different strategy, because the goal of obtaining matter for growth is the same.
senses.whyCN: 植物学家把这个词用于完全不同的策略，因为「获取物质以生长」这一目标是相同的。

senses.title: Public health nutrition
senses.titleCN: 公共营养：人群层面的膳食政策
senses.definition: the population-level field that shapes food supply, fortification and dietary advice
senses.definitionCN: 在人群层面塑造食物供应、营养强化与膳食建议的领域
senses.example: Public health nutrition cut iodine deficiency across the country.
senses.exampleCN: 公共营养工作在全国范围内减少了碘缺乏。
senses.why: The unit of study shifts from a body to a population, and the word scales up with it.
senses.whyCN: 研究对象从个体身体转为整个人群，这个词也随之放大。

senses.title: On the packet
senses.titleCN: 营养标签：包装上的营养成分
senses.definition: the nutrient information printed on food packaging, often headed nutrition facts
senses.definitionCN: 食品包装上印制的养分信息，常以「营养成分表」为标题
senses.example: The nutrition label lists sugar per serving.
senses.exampleCN: 营养标签列出每份的糖含量。
senses.why: Regulation turned the science into a standard table, so the word appears on every packet.
senses.whyCN: 法规把这门科学变成标准表格，因此这个词出现在每个包装上。

senses.title: Nutrition transition
senses.titleCN: 营养转型：人群膳食结构的改变
senses.definition: the shift in a population's diet toward processed food, sugar and fat as incomes rise
senses.definitionCN: 随着收入提高，人群膳食向加工食品、糖与脂肪转变的过程
senses.example: The country's nutrition transition brought rising obesity.
senses.exampleCN: 该国的营养转型带来了肥胖率上升。
senses.why: Epidemiologists needed a name for a society-wide change, so they extended the word with 'transition'.
senses.whyCN: 流行病学家需要为全社会层面的变化命名，便给它加上了 transition。

intro.en: Nutrition comes from Latin nutritio, an action noun from nutrire 'to nourish'. English adopted it in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: nutrition 出自拉丁 nutritio，是动词 nutrire「滋养」构成的行动名词，英语在 16 世纪借入。

items.en: Latin nutrire meant 'to nourish, to suckle'. Its family includes nutriens 'nourishing' and nutritius 'nourishing, nutritious'.
items.cn: 拉丁 nutrire 意为「滋养、哺乳」，其同族词包括 nutriens「滋养的」与 nutritius「有营养的」。

items.en: The action noun nutritio, nutritionis named the act of feeding and the state of being fed, in medical and philosophical Latin.
items.cn: 行动名词 nutritio、nutritionis 在医学与哲学拉丁文中指喂养的动作与被滋养的状态。

items.en: Old French nutrition passed into English in the sixteenth century, first as a medical term for the body's uptake and use of food.
items.cn: 古法语 nutrition 在 16 世纪进入英语，最初是医学术语，指身体摄取与利用食物。

items.en: In the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries the word became the name of a discipline, as calories, vitamins and deficiency diseases were described.
items.cn: 19 世纪至 20 世纪初，随着热量、维生素与缺乏病被描述，这个词成了一门学科的名称。

items.en: Later in the twentieth century nutrition entered policy language through fortification programmes, school meals and labelling rules.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期，营养经强化计划、学校供餐与标签规则进入政策语言。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation of nutrition is uncertain, usually given as the 1550s but not fixed; the earliest uses are translations of Latin medical texts.
items.cn: 来源不确定：nutrition 的英语首见确切书证年代存疑，通常写作 16 世纪 50 年代但并不确定；最早用例是拉丁医学文献的译本。

note.en: The first group holds same-family words that divide the topic differently; the second holds words for what is eaten, how much is eaten, and whether it is enough.
note.cn: 第一组是同族词，但把话题切分得不同；第二组指吃的东西、吃的量以及是否足够。

entries.definition: A single nourishing substance such as a vitamin or an amino acid. Nutrition is the process and the field that study many nutrients together.
entries.definitionCN: 单一种滋养物质，如某种维生素或氨基酸。nutrition 是过程，也是把多种 nutrient 放在一起研究的学科。

entries.definition: An adjective praising food as rich in nutrients. It evaluates a meal, while nutrition names a process or a science.
entries.definitionCN: 称赞食物富含养分的形容词。它评价一餐，而 nutrition 命名过程或学科。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'relating to nutrition', as in nutritional value. It labels the dimension being discussed.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与营养有关的」的形容词，如营养价值。它标明讨论的是哪个维度。

entries.definition: The material or support that keeps something alive. It is more concrete and emotional than the clinical word nutrition.
entries.definitionCN: 维持生命所需的物质或支持。它比临床味更重的 nutrition 更具体、更有情感色彩。

entries.definition: The usual food a person or group eats, or a planned restriction. Nutrition is what the body does with that diet.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或群体常吃的食物，或计划性的限制饮食。nutrition 是身体对这份膳食做了什么。

entries.definition: Poor nutrition caused by too little food or by an unbalanced diet. It is the failure case of nutrition, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 因食物不足或膳食失衡造成的营养不佳。它是营养的反面情形，而非同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin nutrire 'nourish' + -tio: the act of nourishing, turned into a noun.
normal.cn: 拉丁 nutrire「滋养」+ -tio：滋养的动作，再变成名词。

normal.en: The family runs nutrient, nutritional, nutritious, nourish, nutritionist and malnutrition.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 nutrient、nutritional、nutritious、nourish、nutritionist、malnutrition。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: nutrition facts, clinical nutrition, plant nutrition, nutrition education.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：营养成分表、临床营养、植物营养、营养教育。

normal.en: nutrition is the process and the science; a nutrient is one substance.
normal.cn: nutrition 是过程也是学科；nutrient 是某一种物质。

normal.en: Malnutrition is what happens when nutrition fails, not a synonym for it.
normal.cn: malnutrition 是营养失败时的情形，而不是 nutrition 的同义词。

abstract.en: Picture a plate with a child's height marked on the wall behind it, rising year by year.
abstract.cn: 想象一只餐盘，背后墙上画着逐年升高的儿童身高刻度。

abstract.en: Picture a packet turned over to show a grid of numbers headed nutrition facts.
abstract.cn: 想象一个包装袋翻过来，露出一张标题为「营养成分表」的数字表格。

abstract.en: Picture a country's market shelves filling with sweet drinks over a single generation.
abstract.cn: 想象一个国家在一代人的时间里，货架上逐渐堆满含糖饮料。

examples.en: Nutrition is now a compulsory subject for medical students.
examples.cn: 营养学如今是医学生的必修科目。

examples.en: Poor nutrition in the camp weakened the children before the epidemic arrived.
examples.cn: 疫病到来之前，营地里的营养不良已使孩子们虚弱。

examples.en: The study compared the nutrition of urban and rural households.
examples.cn: 这项研究比较了城乡家庭的营养状况。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nutri（滋养）+ tion（过程）」——身体被滋养的全过程 → nutrition 营养

root: 拉丁 nutrire「滋养、哺乳」→ 动作名词 nutritio → 古法语 nutrition → 英语 nutrition。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one process from digestion to a scientific discipline, a diet's quality, a hospital service, a plant's strategy, national policy, a label and a whole society's diet.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一过程从消化走到学科、膳食质量、医院服务、植物策略、国家政策、包装标签，以及整个社会的膳食。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a divided plate beside a textbook and a rising growth curve.
core.cn: 核心意象：分格的餐盘，旁边是一本教科书与上升的生长曲线。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: food is taken in, broken down, absorbed and used.
branches.cn: 过程：食物被摄入、分解、吸收与利用。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE AND STATE: the same noun names the field and the condition of a person's diet.
branches.cn: 知识与状态：同一个名词既指学科，也指一个人膳食的状况。

branches.en: TREATMENT: when eating fails, nutrition becomes a medical procedure.
branches.cn: 治疗：当进食失败时，营养成为医疗规程。

branches.en: PLANTS: another kingdom, the same goal of obtaining matter to grow.
branches.cn: 植物：另一个生物界，同一个「获取物质以生长」的目标。

branches.en: POPULATION AND PACKET: policy, labels and dietary shifts all use the word at scale.
branches.cn: 人群与包装：政策、标签与膳食变迁都在更大尺度上使用这个词。

intro.en: Nutrition is a Latin action noun, and its -tion ending still marks it as a process rather than a thing.
intro.cn: nutrition 是拉丁行动名词，其 -tion 词尾仍标记它是过程而不是实物。

latinIntro.en: Latin -tio produced nutritio; the same ending appears in nutrition's neighbours, oxidation and radiation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 -tio 产生 nutritio；同一词尾也出现在 oxidation、radiation 这些邻近词中。

items.exampleCN: 每种养分的作用各不相同。

items.exampleCN: 加工后营养成分构成改变了。

items.example: The two cereals are nutritionally similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两种麦片在营养上相似。

items.example: The soup is cheap but nutritious.
